Subsequently, model souping is applied to aggregate weights derived from iterative pseudo-labeling. Additionally, cross-domain mixed sampling further enhances detection performance on real data. SIA_Track secured first place in the MOTSynth2MOT17 track at the BMTT 2022 challenge. The source code can be accessed at https://github.com/SIAnalytics/BMTT2022_SIA_track.

Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) utilizing the Bosch process is a fundamental technique for fabricating micron-scale structures in silicon for MEMS and microfluidics, playing a critical role in advancing biomedical research miniaturization. Although this method ensures high aspect ratios and design versatility, it is typically hindered by etch lag and dependence on intricate oxide masks for achieving depth. This study presents an optimized Bosch process that lowers etch lag to under 1.5%. Additionally, we refined a three-step Bosch approach, successfully enabling the creation of stable structures with a thickness of 6 micrometers at depths reaching up to 180 micrometers.

For any integer $k \ge 2$, a set $A$ of positive integers is termed an asymptotic basis of order $k$ if sufficiently large positive integers can be expressed as the sum of $k$ elements from $A$. A set $A$ is defined as a Sidon set when all pairwise sums of its elements are distinct. Long ago, P. Erdős, A. Sárközy, and V. T. Sós questioned the existence of a Sidon set that serves as an asymptotic basis of order 3. In this work, we demonstrate the existence of such a Sidon set $A$ possessing a positive lower density within its three-fold sumset $A + A + A$, utilizing probabilistic techniques.

This study examines a specific issue in query-based object detectors where predictions are accurate during intermediate decoding stages but fail at the final stage. After analyzing the training methodology, we identify two root causes: insufficient training focus on later stages and error propagation through the decoding sequence. To address this, we propose Selective Query Recollection (SQR), a straightforward and effective training strategy. SQR accumulates intermediate queries as decoding progresses and selectively routes them to subsequent stages, bypassing the strict sequential flow. This approach prioritizes training emphasis on later stages and enables them to directly utilize queries from earlier phases. SQR is easily integrated into various query-based detectors without altering the inference pipeline, resulting in consistent performance gains of 1.4–2.8 AP when applied to Adamixer, DAB-DETR, and Deformable-DETR across diverse configurations.

Style transfer has garnered significant recent interest; however, while much of this research focuses on accelerating processing, existing methods lack a principled art historical foundation. A style encompasses more than a single image or artist, yet prior work is often restricted to one instance or fails to leverage multiple images. Furthermore, previous approaches have relied on direct comparisons within the RGB domain or utilized CNNs pre-trained on ImageNet, which depends on millions of labeled bounding boxes and may introduce bias due to its lack of artistic consideration. To address these limitations, we introduce a style-aware content loss trained jointly with a deep encoder-decoder network for real-time, high-resolution stylization of both images and videos. We also propose a quantitative metric to assess stylization quality and have art historians rank patches generated by our method against those from prior work. Our qualitative and quantitative results, ranging from small patches to megapixel-scale images and videos, demonstrate that our approach more effectively captures the subtle ways in which style influences content.

Neural Machine Translation usually relies on the premise that the translation with the highest predicted probability corresponds to the highest human-rated quality. This study challenges that notion, demonstrating that model confidence and actual translation quality exhibit only a weak correlation. We propose an alternative inference method using Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding on unbiased samples to optimize various automated quality metrics, rather than relying on the traditional beam search approach. While beam search selects hypotheses with the greatest model probability, MBR decoding prioritizes those with the highest estimated quality. Our experiments reveal that combining a neural translation model with the neural reference-based metric BLEURT significantly boosts human evaluation scores. Notably, these improved results are achieved using translations that differ from standard beam-search outputs; specifically, these translations possess considerably lower model likelihood and are less favored by surface-level metrics such as BLEU.

Spontaneous symmetry breaking underpins the diverse phenomena observed in equilibrium physics. Pushing a system into a non-equilibrium state greatly expands the potential for such symmetry breaking, allowing it to manifest not only spatially but also temporally. This research examines a driven-dissipative frustrated magnetic system, revealing that frustration within this far-from-equilibrium environment can generate a variety of fascinating non-equilibrium phases characterized by intertwined space-time symmetry breaking. For instance, a discrete time crystal phase emerges alongside a time-dependent spatial order that oscillates between a long-range tripartite stripe and a short-range ferromagnetic configuration.

We derive a series of consistency findings regarding trees and stationary reflection at double successors of regular cardinals $\kappa$, thereby refining certain classical constructions. These results encompass models satisfying $\mathsf{CSR}(\kappa^{++}) \wedge \mathsf{TP}(\kappa^{++})$ (with or without $\mathsf{AP}(\kappa^{++})$), as well as models for the combinations $\mathsf{SR}(\kappa^{++}) \wedge \mathsf{wTP}(\kappa^{++}) \wedge \mathsf{AP}(\kappa^{++})$ and $\neg \mathsf{AP}(\kappa^{++}) \wedge \mathsf{SR}(\kappa^{++})$. The latter scenario, previously established by Krueger and the first author via \cite{GilKru:8fold}, is now demonstrated using alternative techniques. Additionally, we present analogous outcomes involving the failure of $\mathsf{SH}(\kappa^{++})$. Finally, leveraging recent collaborative work by Honzik and the third author, we achieve all these results under the condition of an arbitrarily large $2^\kappa$.

We introduce a new method for generating sign language videos using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Building on Stoll et al.'s prior research, we leverage the human semantic parser of the Soft-Gated Warping-GAN to create photorealistic videos driven by region-level spatial layouts. Enhancing the synthesis of target poses yields improved performance across independent and contrasting signers. Consequently, our system was evaluated on the highly diverse MS-ASL dataset, which includes over 200 signers, achieving an SSIM score of 0.893. Additionally, we present a periodic weighting strategy for the generator that reactivates training and produces quantitatively superior outcomes.

Cable-driven soft robots featuring redundant degrees of freedom can execute trajectory tracking while simultaneously satisfying additional constraints, such as maintaining a specific end-effector orientation or avoiding collisions with obstacles. These requirements necessitate strategic motion planning. This study derives compressible curvature kinematics for cable-driven soft robots, explicitly accounting for the compressibility of soft segments. We investigated motion planning strategies for these robots under constrained conditions, including fixed end-effector orientations and obstacle avoidance. The inverse kinematics for cable actuation were formulated as a damped least-squares optimization problem and solved iteratively in an offline environment. Both simulation results (provided as open-source) and prototype experiments evaluated the system's trajectory tracking accuracy and adherence to constraints. Furthermore, this approach can be extended to similar multi-segment cable-driven soft robotic systems by customizing parameters to facilitate prior motion planning.

This paper explores intrinsically flat spacetimes as viable cosmological models. We demonstrate that they possess a natural geometric structure capable of describing inhomogeneous matter distributions arranged in a periodic pattern across space. We establish theorems regarding their local representation, as well as the existence and uniqueness of Einstein's equations under these periodic boundary conditions. Furthermore, we identify a significant class of exact solutions that highlight the utility of such spacetimes in cosmology, exhibiting early-time behavior approaching homogeneity and isotropy, alongside late-time characteristics featuring peaks and voids in matter distribution.

A core principle of the AdS/CFT correspondence is that specific geometric features of a bulk state are represented by the entanglement structure of its dual boundary counterpart. Since entanglement is not a linear quantum observable, geometry within a quantum theory of gravity must similarly lack linearity, permitting linear dependencies among states with distinct geometries. This study investigates such dependencies between states possessing simple geometric duals: specifically, configurations composed of $n$ copies of a thermofield double state and those derived by permuting the $n$ right-hand components. There are $n!$ such states, each corresponding to a unique geometry. We calculate the maximum fidelity between one state and a linear combination of the others, finding that this fidelity approaches 1 as the number $n$ of black holes grows. Additionally, we examine whether a single thermofield double state can emerge as the partial trace of a superposition of states whose topology does not connect the two untraced sides. We establish lower bounds for the fidelity between the thermofield double state and these partial traces and discuss the conceptual ramifications of their existence.

DNA operates within the restricted environment of the cell. Intensive investigation into the transcription and replication of DNA under such confinement is structurally crucial for controlling DNA self-assembly within chambers or channels. This study examines double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) molecules of varying lengths and sequences to assess their thermal stability within a conically shaped confined space. Employing the Peyrard-Bishop-Dauxois (PBD) model, we calculate the melting profile of dsDNA confined against one side of a conical wall, which simulates cellular boundaries. Our findings indicate that both the confinement itself and the specific geometry of the space significantly influence the molecule's stability.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) has recently seen remarkable advancements in multi-agent settings, yet training on increasingly complex tasks remains computationally expensive and resource-intensive. To address this bottleneck, efficiently leveraging historical experience is crucial, a challenge that has been under-explored because existing methods often fail in continuously varying environments due to their intricate designs. This paper introduces "KnowRU," a knowledge reusing method designed for easy integration into most multi-agent RL algorithms without requiring complex manual engineering. By utilizing knowledge distillation to transfer information among agents, KnowRU aims to accelerate training on new tasks while enhancing asymptotic performance. Extensive experiments on state-of-the-art Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithms across both collaborative and competitive scenarios demonstrate the method's robustness and effectiveness. The results indicate that KnowRU surpasses recent approaches, highlighting the critical value of knowledge reusing in MARL.

Protein-DNA interactions are essential for the operation of all natural systems, with the protein's search for specific DNA sites playing a pivotal role. While this topic has been investigated for decades, recent advances have clarified its microscopic details. This paper reviews the current theoretical insights into the molecular mechanisms governing the protein target search. We introduce and elucidate a comprehensive discrete-state stochastic method to model the dynamics of these search phenomena. Our theoretical framework employs first-passage analysis and incorporates key physical-chemical processes, successfully capturing remarkable features of the protein search, such as exceptionally high effective association rates, high selectivity and specificity, and robustness against crowding and sequence heterogeneity.

This study introduces the concepts of decisional width for finite relational structures and for regular classes of finite structures. Our primary finding demonstrates that for a first-order formula $\psi$ over a vocabulary $\tau$ and a finite automaton $F$ representing a width-$w$ regular-decisional class of $\tau$-structures, it is possible to determine in time $f(\tau, \Sigma, \psi, w)|F|$ whether any structure in the class satisfies $\psi$. The function $f$ relies on the parameters $\tau, \Sigma, \psi,$ and $w$, but remains independent of the automaton $F$'s size. Consequently, this result not only confirms that the first-order theory of any regular-decisional class of finite structures is decidable but also establishes that, with fixed parameters $\tau, \psi, \Sigma,$ and $w$, decidability can be achieved in linear time relative to the automaton $F$. Furthermore, extending our main proof, we demonstrate that counting the satisfying assignments of a first-order logic formula within a structure $A$ of width $w$ is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to $w$, solvable in quadratic time based on the input representation's length.

Assessing task similarity is essential across a wide range of machine learning domains, such as transfer, multi-task, continual, and meta-learning. However, existing methods are largely architecture-dependent, either relying on pre-trained models or using forward transfer as a proxy after training networks on specific tasks. This paper introduces a novel, model-agnostic, and training-free task embedding for supervised classification based on optimal transport theory, capable of managing partially disjoint label sets. Specifically, we generate label embeddings via multi-dimensional scaling, concatenate these with dataset samples, and define the distance between two datasets as their 2-Wasserstein distance. We further utilize a 2-Wasserstein embedding framework to map tasks into a vector space where Euclidean distances approximate the proposed 2-Wasserstein distances between tasks. Our approach enables significantly faster task comparisons than related methods like the Optimal Transport Dataset Distance (OTDD). Additionally, numerical experiments confirm the embedding's effectiveness, revealing statistically significant correlations between our proposed distance metric and both forward and backward transfer performance.

The formation and stability of filamentary dust structures, often referred to as "chains," are primarily governed by the dynamic interplay between individual charged grains and the intricate electric potential generated by local plasma charge distributions. Recent findings from the Plasmakristall-4 (PK-4) experiment on the International Space Station (ISS) reveal that the positive column of the gas discharge plasma hosts rapid ionization waves. These waves cause plasma parameters to fluctuate by up to an order of magnitude from their average background values. Such a highly variable environment likely significantly influences dust particle dynamics and self-organization, especially regarding chain formation and stability. In this study, we analyze the electric potential around dust chains in PK-4 using a molecular dynamics model for dust and ions, informed by boundary conditions from a Particle-in-Cell with Monte Carlo collisions (PIC-MCC) simulation of ionization waves. We examine how plasma conditions within different regions of these waves affect dust structures, contrasting them with results derived from time-averaged plasma conditions. Comparing our simulated chains with PK-4 experimental data demonstrates that time-averaged conditions fail to accurately reproduce observed dust behavior, underscoring the need for more precise modeling of plasma conditions when ionization waves are present. Furthermore, we show that standard analytic expressions for electric potential are insufficient for accurately describing the potential near charged dust grains under these specific plasma conditions.

We investigate Hilbert spaces $H$ interpreted within a first-order theory. By introducing a novel finiteness condition termed {\em scatteredness}, we demonstrate that $H$ decomposes into a direct sum of {\em asymptotically free} components, characterized by short-range interactions governed by algebraic closure and the absence of long-range interactions. This framework encompasses $L^2$-spaces associated with Macpherson-Steinhorn definable measures, $L^2$ spaces linked to the Haar measure of absolute Galois groups, irreducible unitary representations of $p$-adic Lie groups, and unitary representations of the automorphism group of an $\omega$-categorical theory. In the latter scenario, our primary result aligns with a theorem established by Tsankov. The proof necessitates novel techniques, specifically leveraging local stability theory within continuous logic.

This study investigates how specific 2HDM models, namely SM and Model III, influence the polarized and unpolarized forward-backward asymmetries in the decays $\overline{B}\rightarrow \overline{K}_0^{*}(1430) \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\overline{B}\rightarrow \overline{K} \ell^+\ell^-$. We compare the results derived from these decay channels and determine the minimum event counts necessary to observe each asymmetry, contrasting these requirements with the projected $B\bar{B}$ production rates at the LHC and the Super-LHC. Ultimately, we conclude that analyzing these asymmetries in the $\overline{B}\rightarrow \overline{K}_0^*(1430) \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\overline{B}\rightarrow \overline{K} \ell^+\ell^-$ processes offers highly effective means for discovering new physics in future B-physics experiments.

This study addresses the challenge of generating conditional synthetic data for a target domain without access to its labels or attributes. We introduce a transfer learning framework that combines normalizing flows with both maximum-likelihood and adversarial training strategies. The approach models a source domain with available labels and a target domain lacking them using separate normalizing flows, achieving domain alignment within a shared latent space through adversarial discriminators. Leveraging the invertible nature of flow models ensures exact cycle consistency in the mapping. Furthermore, we employ an encoder trained via adversarial methods to learn the joint distribution of data and attributes in the source domain, mapping attributes into the latent space. During synthesis, the method produces target domain samples conditioned on any specified attribute combination. Empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets validate the method's effectiveness. We anticipate this approach will be highly valuable for label-scarce systems, offering non-trivial data augmentations through attribute transformations. Unlike standard geometric and photometric changes, these synthetic samples introduce greater entropy into the target domain, thereby enhancing robustness for downstream tasks.

Probabilistic time series forecasting, which entails predicting the distribution of future values based on historical data, is crucial for risk management in downstream decisions. We introduce a deep state space model for this purpose, utilizing neural networks to parameterize both the non-linear emission and transition models, while employing recurrent neural networks to capture dependencies. Adopting the automatic relevance determination (ARD) perspective, we develop a network that leverages exogenous variables alongside time series data. Specifically, our ARD framework integrates the uncertainty inherent in exogenous variables, aiding in the identification of relevant factors while suppressing irrelevant ones. Multi-step forecast distributions are approximated through Monte Carlo simulation. Experimental results demonstrate that our model generates accurate and sharp probabilistic forecasts, with estimated uncertainty increasing realistically and spontaneously over time.

This paper focuses on a (strong) Morse function defined on a compact manifold with boundary. We establish a corresponding cellular structure and analyze its algebraic characteristics. Additionally, we provide an estimate addressing Arnold's inquiry regarding the number of critical points of a Morse function subject to specific boundary conditions.

Data has emerged as a limitation in deep learning. Experts across various domains believe that "deep neural networks do not necessarily improve with increased data," yet this notion remains unvalidated experimentally and lacks a robust theoretical framework. To address this gap, we conduct experiments under Identically Independent Distribution (IID) and Out of Distribution (OOD) conditions, yielding significant insights. Guided by these findings, we propose two theories: under IID settings, sample effectiveness is governed by information quantity, where sample contribution and inter-class differences dictate the volume of sample and class information; under OOD settings, sample contributions are determined by the degree of cross-domain divergence, with bias-fitting from irrelevant elements acting as a critical factor. These data-centric theories offer valuable guidance, fostering broader practical applications of artificial intelligence.

As system complexity and attack sophistication grow, the need for autonomous cyber defense in cyber and cyber-physical systems (CPSs) has become increasingly evident. However, many current state-of-the-art frameworks either depend on static models with unrealistic assumptions or fail to meet essential safety and security requirements. This paper introduces a novel hybrid autonomous agent architecture designed to optimize and verify reinforcement learning (RL) defense policies by integrating constraint verification via satisfiability modulo theory (SMT) into the agent's decision-making loop. Incorporating SMT not only guarantees the satisfaction of safety and security constraints but also delivers continuous feedback to guide the RL agent toward safe and effective actions. This methodology is crucial for CPSs that face high risks from potential safety or security breaches. Evaluation of this approach in a simulated CPS environment demonstrates that the agent rapidly learns an optimal policy and successfully counters diverse attack strategies in 99% of cases.

The maximum independent set problem stands as a pivotal challenge in graph algorithms, having been thoroughly investigated within the context of worst-case analysis for exact algorithms addressing NP-hard problems. In its weighted variant, every vertex carries a specific weight, and the objective is to identify an independent set that maximizes the sum of these weights. This paper introduces multiple reduction rules alongside a rapid exact algorithm tailored for the maximum weighted independent set problem, employing the measure-and-conquer method to determine the algorithm's running time complexity. Applicable to general weighted graphs, the proposed method demonstrates particularly efficient performance on sparse graphs. Specifically, when the average degree of the graph does not exceed 3, the algorithm executes in $O^*(1.1443^n)$ time with polynomial space requirements, thereby surpassing prior time complexity bounds established for cubic graphs under polynomial space constraints.

We investigate the chain of Alexander duals $(I_n^\vee)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ arising from an ascending sequence of $\Sym$-invariant squarefree monomial ideals $(I_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. By introducing a new combinatorial concept termed \emph{avoidance up to symmetry}, we explicitly characterize the minimal generating set of the duals up to symmetry based on the original generators. Integrating this finding with discrete geometry techniques, we demonstrate that for sufficiently large $n$, the count of orbit generators for $I_n^\vee$ follows a polynomial in $n$. Similarly, the number of orbit generators of minimal degree eventually becomes a linear function of $n$. Consequently, the number of $\Sym$-orbits of primary components of $I_n$ grows polynomially with $n$ for large values. Additionally, we establish that for every $i\geq 0$, the number of $i$-dimensional faces in the associated Stanley-Reisner complexes of $I_n$ is also described by a polynomial in $n$ for large $n$.

The triad census is a vital method in network science for analyzing local structures, offering a complete overview of relational patterns among triples of actors. However, researchers frequently require an integration of relational ties with categorical node attributes. Consequently, it is essential to incorporate node labels, or colors, into the triad census framework. This paper presents an efficient algorithm for generating a colored triad census, which builds upon techniques used for the traditional triad census. We assess the algorithm's performance using both empirical and simulated data for undirected and directed graphs. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method significantly reduces computational time compared to naive approaches. Furthermore, we apply the colored triad census to the Zachary karate club network. This application not only highlights the algorithm's efficiency but also demonstrates a statistical testing procedure by creating a null distribution through 1,000 realizations of a mixing-matrix conditioned graph to compare observed counts against expected values. These findings support our analysis of homophily, heterophily, and bridging. In conclusion, the proposed algorithm for the colored triad census offers novel and efficient capabilities for social network analysis.

This paper utilizes KAM theory and Aubry-Mather theory for twist maps to investigate the bound geodesic dynamics of a perturbed black hole background. These general theories primarily address two observable phenomena: the photon shell (characterized by unstable bound spherical orbits) and quasi-periodic oscillations. Our findings reveal a gap structure within the photon shell that can expose details about the perturbation.

Utilizing the sheaf cohomology BGG technique introduced by the authors and Lachowska-Qi, we calculate the Hochschild cohomology groups for several blocks within the small quantum group. Our findings regarding the centers of these blocks align with the conjectures proposed by Lachowska-Qi. Specifically, for the nontrivial singular block where $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{sl}_3$, we determine the $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{N}]$-module structure of HH*$(\mathfrak{u}_{\lambda})$.

This work investigates how leptophilic dark matter interactions affect the decays of muons and ground-state mesons observed in current experiments. We examine a secluded dark sector that couples solely to leptons through either a scalar or vector mediator, thereby modifying leptonic decay processes and distorting their energy spectra. Initially, we analyze the Michel decay of muons ($\mu^+ightarrow e^+
u_e  ar{
u}_\mu$), which provides relatively robust constraints on the model's parameter space. Subsequently, we explore rare decays of $\pi^\pm$, $K^\pm$, $D^\pm$, and $D_s^\pm$ into $e
u$. The presence of scalar mediators would eliminate Standard Model helicity suppression, enabling the derivation of stringent limits. However, the resulting bounds on light mediator couplings to electrons and muons remain somewhat weaker than those obtained from low-energy $e^+e^-$ collider searches and muon magnetic moment measurements, respectively. Finally, we demonstrate that pion and kaon decays effectively rule out a "Co-SIMP" scenario involving a scalar dark matter particle with a dimension-5 coupling to electrons.

Contact tracing has become a globally implemented strategy to curb the spread of COVID-19. Leveraging digital technologies like smartphones and wearables, health authorities can efficiently identify and notify individuals potentially exposed to the virus. Consequently, numerous mobile applications have been created for this purpose. Nevertheless, significant concerns persist regarding the operational mechanisms and performance of these tools. While existing literature offers exploratory insights into public reception through news analysis and user reviews, no current solution automatically processes these reviews to extract sentiments. This study introduces a pipeline that begins with manual annotation via a crowdsourcing initiative and culminates in the development and training of AI models for automatic sentiment analysis. Employing eight distinct methods, we achieved an average F1-Score of 94.8%, demonstrating the viability of automated sentiment analysis for COVID-19 contact tracing apps. Furthermore, we identify key advantages, limitations, and user concerns associated with these applications. Additionally, we have assembled and manually annotated a large-scale dataset comprising 34,534 reviews from contact tracing applications across 46 different countries. The analysis and dataset presented herein are intended to serve as a baseline and benchmark for future research in this field.

Gas cycling within the circumgalactic regions of galaxies is recognized as a multi-phase phenomenon. The MUSE-ALMA Haloes survey aims to significantly deepen our understanding of the physical characteristics of this circumgalactic medium (CGM) gas by assembling a substantial multi-wavelength dataset comprising both absorption and emission observations. A central element of this survey is a coordinated observational campaign utilizing VLT/MUSE, ALMA, and HST. The absorber-selected targets include 19 VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy quasar fields, featuring 32 strong absorbers with redshifts $z_{\rm abs}<$0.85 and neutral hydrogen column densities ($N_{HI}$) $\geq 10^{18}$ cm$^{\rm -2}$ identified via UV-spectroscopy. Complementing this, a new HST medium program employs a 40-orbit sequence of three-band imaging using UVIS and IR WFC3 to characterize the stellar populations of the host galaxies. In addition to these absorber-selected targets, the combined fields reveal 3,658 sources, of which 703 have spectroscopic redshifts; this galaxy-selected sample forms the primary subject of the current paper. Millimeter-wave ALMA observations have been secured for select fields to investigate the molecular gas properties of these objects. This paper details the survey's scientific objectives, target selection criteria, observational strategy, data processing methods, and source identification procedures for the entire sample. Furthermore, we present catalogs of photometric measurements for all objects detected in VLT/MUSE, ALMA, and HST broad-band images, along with associated spectroscopic redshifts derived from VLT/MUSE data. Collectively, this comprehensive dataset enables a robust characterization of neutral atomic gas, molecular gas, and stellar content within the same objects, facilitating a baryon census of condensed matter in complex galaxy structures.

The second section addresses the construction of a spectrum linked to a multi-adjunction scenario. By leveraging a geometric perspective on its multi-versal nature, an object's spectrum is defined as spaces of local units endowed with a topology derived from orthogonality. Following a review of Diers' original framework, this paper presents novel contributions. Initially, it clarifies how a multi-adjunction can be refined into an adjunction between categories of modeled spaces, consistent with the topos-theoretic method. Subsequently, it examines the 2-functorial dimensions of this process within a 2-category of Diers contexts. Furthermore, the work proposes an axiomatization of spectral duality via morphisms of fibrations over a category of spatial objects and demonstrates how these configurations yield right multi-adjoint functors.

Given the anticipated increase in frequency and intensity of wildfires, developing enhanced prediction models is essential for risk mitigation and resource allocation. Leveraging remote sensing data enables the creation of valuable spatiotemporal statistical models to support resource management. This paper introduces a dynamic model for forecasting future wildfires across five locations in the western United States, utilizing a deep neural network trained on historical burned area and climate data. The proposed approach incorporates distinct features tailored to prediction evaluation needs, specifically dynamic online estimation and time-series modeling. Across these locations, local fire triggers are interconnected rather than isolated, and analyzing local data presents confounding factors due to incomplete state observations. Compared to existing methods that fail to account for incomplete state observations in wildfire time-series data, our approach achieves superior prediction performance on average.

This study addresses the integration of Energy-based Models (EBMs) as guiding priors for motion optimization. EBMs utilize neural networks to represent expressive probability density distributions through a Gibbs distribution parameterized by an energy function. Their implicit nature allows for straightforward integration as optimization factors or initial sampling distributions, making them ideal for incorporating data-driven priors into motion optimization tasks. This work outlines the necessary modeling and algorithmic adaptations to apply EBMs in this context. We examine the advantages of adding regularizers during EBM learning for use with gradient-based optimizers and introduce several EBM architectures capable of learning generalizable distributions for manipulation tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate multiple scenarios for integrating EBMs into motion optimization and evaluate the performance of learned models as guiding priors in both simulated environments and real-world robotic experiments.

Ferromagnetic topological insulators (FM TIs) are promising for high-precision metrology, edge-channel spintronics, and hosting chiral Majorana zero modes for topological qubits when paired with superconductors. Although the Mn-based A1B2C4 stoichiometry was recently identified as a stable route to intrinsic magnetic TIs, the primary candidate, MnBi2Te4, is limited by its antiferromagnetic nature (25 K Néel temperature) and strong n-type doping. This study demonstrates that p-type MnSb2Te4, previously thought to be topologically trivial, becomes a ferromagnetic topological insulator upon introducing a few percent excess of Mn. Key findings include: (i) a ferromagnetic hysteresis with a record Curie temperature of 45–50 K, (ii) out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy, and (iii) a two-dimensional Dirac cone situated near the Fermi level. Spectroscopic analyses further reveal (iv) out-of-plane spin polarization and (v) a magnetically induced band gap that vanishes at the Curie temperature. Additionally, a critical magnetization exponent of β ≈ 1 suggests proximity to a quantum critical point. Ab initio calculations indicate that substituting Sb with excess Mn atoms drives the ferromagnetic interlayer coupling. The resulting deviations from perfect ferromagnetic order open an inverted bulk band gap, establishing MnSb2Te4 as a robust topological insulator and a new benchmark in the field of magnetic topological materials.

This study investigates control issues associated with fractional non-instantaneous impulsive functional evolution equations featuring state-dependent delays and Caputo fractional derivatives within Banach spaces. The primary aim is to establish sufficient conditions ensuring the approximate controllability of such systems in separable reflexive Banach spaces. To accomplish this, we employ the resolvent operator method alongside Schauder's fixed point theorem in our proofs. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of approximate controllability for linear systems, addressing a gap in current literature. An illustrative example is included to demonstrate the validity of our findings. Additionally, we highlight specific limitations in existing research regarding the characterization of mild solutions, phase spaces, and the approximate controllability of fractional-order impulsive systems in Banach spaces.

We report exact diagonalization findings for finite clusters within a spin-1/2 $t$-$J$ model featuring random all-to-all hopping and exchange interactions. We contend that these random models effectively capture the essential strong local correlations required for describing cuprates and similar materials, without introducing lattice symmetry-breaking orders. The spin glass ordered phase, previously identified in the insulating regime at doping $p=0$, persists into a metallic spin glass phase up to a transition point at $p_c \approx 1/3$. Near $p_c$, the dynamic spin susceptibility exhibits characteristics reminiscent of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model spectrum. Additionally, the phase transition is indicated by peaks in entropy, entanglement entropy, and compressibility. Finally, the electron energy distribution in the metallic phase ($p>p_c$) aligns with a disordered extension of the Luttinger-volume Fermi surface, a relationship that fails when $p<p_c$.

The Steiner tree enumeration problem is a recognized challenge focused on identifying all Steiner trees. While many theoretical studies have developed algorithms and analyzed their complexity for this issue, no practical approaches or experimental evaluations have existed to date. This paper addresses the Steiner tree enumeration problem through a practical lens. We introduce a cost-constrained minimal Steiner tree enumeration problem, which seeks to list all minimal Steiner trees with costs below a specified limit. To solve this, we present an algorithm based on Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs). This method constructs a BDD that compactly encodes the set of minimal Steiner trees and subsequently traverses it to perform enumeration. We also devise a new *frontier-based algorithm* to efficiently build these BDDs. Our traversal technique eliminates Steiner trees exceeding the cost threshold. Furthermore, we enhance the algorithm by preprocessing the input graph and regulating the count of generated trees to lower memory and computational demands. This extension improves scalability by producing a subset of the minimal Steiner trees. Our validation demonstrates that the proposed algorithm enumerates Steiner trees in real-world graphs more efficiently than current methods.

Accurately setting sales prices is critical for businesses, making the study and forecasting of price time series a vital topic from both economic and data science standpoints. This paper investigates various techniques for predicting sales prices used by an Italian food wholesaler, aiming to automate tasks currently performed by human staff. We evaluate ARIMA models against Prophet, a scalable tool from Facebook based on generalized additive models, and deep learning architectures utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). ARIMA serves as a standard benchmark in econometric analysis. Our findings show that ARIMA and LSTM networks yield comparable performance, whereas the combination of CNNs and LSTMs achieves the highest overall accuracy, albeit with a longer tuning process. In contrast, Prophet is fast and user-friendly but significantly less accurate.

Image segmentation and restoration are pivotal areas in image processing that have yielded significant advancements. This paper introduces a novel multiphase segmentation framework that integrates both image restoration and segmentation techniques. By leveraging restoration principles, the proposed model robustly handles challenging inputs such as high-noise, blurry, pixel-deficient, and vector-valued images. Specifically, the widely used piecewise constant Mumford-Shah model is readily extended to segment gray and vector-valued images corrupted by noise, blur, or missing data by coupling a new data fidelity term derived from image restoration. This approach can be efficiently solved via an alternating minimization algorithm, whose convergence is proven for a three-variable system under mild conditions. Experimental results on diverse synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art segmentation models, particularly in dealing with blurry images and those containing missing pixel values.

Although reinforcement learning (RL) theoretically enables robots to autonomously adjust to new tasks, existing RL approaches demand extensive trial counts to achieve this. This paper addresses the challenge of rapid task adaptation using meta-learning, specifically tailored for industrial insertion operations. Rapid adaptation is essential because the prohibitive number of trials required by standard methods risks damaging hardware, yet effective adaptation is viable because experiences across various insertion applications are highly transferable. In this context, we resolve two key obstacles inherent to meta-learning. First, traditional meta-RL algorithms necessitate lengthy online training; we demonstrate that this can be substituted with carefully selected offline data, creating an offline meta-RL framework that relies solely on demonstrations and trials from previous tasks, eliminating the need for expensive online procedures. Second, meta-RL often struggles to generalize to novel tasks that differ significantly from those encountered during meta-training, a critical issue in industrial settings where high success rates are paramount. We overcome this by integrating contextual meta-learning with direct online fine-tuning: the contextual learner adapts instantly when a new task resembles prior data, whereas it gradually fine-tunes when the task is too distinct. Our approach successfully adapts to diverse insertion tasks with a 100% success rate using only a fraction of the samples required for learning from scratch. Experiment videos and further details are accessible at https://sites.google.com/view/offline-metarl-insertion.

This study examines deterministic SIS dynamics on extensive networks, initiating from a minimal number of infected nodes. Under mild assumptions, we demonstrate that any two epidemic trajectories on the same network with identical parameters are nearly identical, up to a time shift, provided the initial conditions are sufficiently small, irrespective of the specific initial infection distribution. We identify the limit of an epidemic originating from the infinite past with infinitesimal prevalence as a nontrivial eternal solution that bridges the disease-free state and the endemic equilibrium. This framework encompasses several benchmark models, including the N-Intertwined Mean Field Approximation (NIMFA) and the Inhomogeneous Mean Field Approximation (IMFA).

This work investigates the invisible scalar particle $S$ within charmed meson and baryon decays involving flavor-changing neutral currents (FCNCs), utilizing a model-independent effective Lagrangian describing the interaction between quarks and the scalar. Leveraging constraints on coupling constants derived from the recent BES III experiment on the $D^{0}\to\pi^{0}\bar\nu\nu$ decay, we forecast that the branching ratios for the processes $D^{+}\to\pi^{+}S$, $D_s^+\to K^+S$, $\Lambda_c\to pS$, $\Xi_c^{0(+)}\to \Sigma^{0(+)}S$, and $\Xi_c^0\to\Lambda S$ could reach values of $10.6,~2.53,~2.39,~0.963,~5.77$, and $2.92\times10^{-4}$, respectively, assuming a scalar mass of approximately $1.1~{\rm GeV}$. Several of these decay channels are within reach for current facilities like BES III, LHCb, and Belle II, as well as upcoming projects such as FCC-ee.

We demonstrate that the earthquake flow exhibits at most polynomial mixing, where the degree is constrained by a constant determined solely by the surface's topology. Consequently, it does not display exponential mixing.

Self-organized semiconductor quantum dots function as nearly ideal two-level systems, offering significant promise for photonic quantum technologies, particularly as emitters for near-perfect quantum light sources. Their potential is further amplified in coupled configurations, which can host highly stable singlet-triplet spin qubits for efficient spin-photon interfaces and enable deterministic generation of photonic 2D cluster states. This study presents an advanced quantum dot molecule (QDM) device featuring electrically tunable QDMs formed by stacked quantum dots within a pin-diode architecture. These QDMs were deterministically embedded into a photonic structure containing a circular Bragg grating via in-situ electron beam lithography. Measurements reveal a photon extraction efficiency reaching up to (24$\pm$4)%, consistent with numerical simulations. Bias voltage-dependent spectroscopy confirms the coupling characteristics of the QDMs, allowing control over orbital couplings and charge states with quantitative alignment to theoretical predictions. Furthermore, the devices exhibit superior single-photon emission properties, characterized by a multi-photon suppression factor of $g^{(2)}(0) = (3.9 \pm 0.5) \cdot 10^{-3}$. These performance metrics position the developed QDM devices as compelling components for future photonic quantum networks utilizing sophisticated nanophotonic hardware.

Although the standard model remains the most successful framework for describing elementary particle interactions and constituents, it has been rigorously tested for over forty years. Weak decays of charm quarks offer an ideal means to probe the coupling strengths between quark families and investigate CP violation. As the lightest charm-strange baryons containing three distinct flavors, $\Xi_c$ baryons (composed of $csu$ or $csd$) have been the subject of extensive experimental investigation at both the Large Hadron Collider and electron-positron colliders. Nevertheless, a significant gap in theoretical reliability continues to hinder progress. To address this, we employ cutting-edge Lattice QCD methods to generate 2+1 clover fermion ensembles across two lattice spacings, $a=(0.108{\rm fm},0.080{\rm fm})$. We subsequently report the first {\it ab-initio} lattice QCD calculation of the form factors governing the $\Xi_{c}\to \Xi \ell^+\nu_{\ell}$ transition, a process analogous to nuclear $\beta$-decay. Our theoretical predictions for decay widths align with recent experimental data from the ALICE and Belle collaborations while offering approximately double the precision. When combined with these experimental results, we independently extract the quark-mixing matrix element $|V_{cs}|$, yielding a value consistent with other independent determinations.

We introduce two key contributions: a) LAST, an end-to-end Speech Translation model that is language-agnostic, and b) a data augmentation strategy designed to enhance performance in code-switching (CS) scenarios. As globalization progresses, fluent speech increasingly involves the interchangeable use of multiple languages. This code-switching complicates traditional speech recognition and translation pipelines, which require identifying the spoken language first before applying language-specific recognizers and translation components to produce the target output. Such sequential processing introduces latency and errors. To address this, we propose a unified end-to-end approach that treats speech recognition and translation as a single problem. By training LAST on both input languages, the model decodes speech directly into a target language irrespective of the source language. While LAST achieves accuracy in monolingual settings comparable to existing methods, it significantly reduces latency and error rates when handling code-switched speech.

Using Evans-Kishimoto's intertwining argument, we classify actions of discrete amenable groups on the normalizer of a full group associated with an ergodic transformation. Our proof remains independent of the specific types of ergodic transformations involved.

Learning graphons has garnered significant interest from various scientific fields, with notable advancements recently made in sparse settings. However, existing methods still necessitate diverging degrees to function efficiently when the local graph structure is homogeneous. This paper introduces an efficient algorithm capable of learning graphons within the constant expected degree regime. The proposed algorithm successfully estimates the rank-$k$ projection of a graphon in the $L_2$ metric, provided that the top $k$ eigenvalues of the graphon adhere to a generalized Kesten-Stigum condition.

Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) serve as a probe for the high-redshift universe, with the Amati relation—linking the isotropic equivalent radiant energy ($E_{iso}$) to the spectral peak energy in the GRB rest frame ($E_p$)—acting as a distance indicator. To address the circularity problem caused by the scarcity of low-redshift GRBs, researchers have developed model-independent methods. In this study, we employ Hubble parameter measurements derived from the differential ages of galaxies to bypass this circularity. Specifically, we apply a non-parametric Gaussian Process approach to observational Hubble data, avoiding assumptions about cosmological models or parameters, to determine luminosity distances required for calculating $E_{iso}$. Our results show that the best-fit parameters of the Amati relation align with previous findings.

This study presents the initial measurements of J/$\psi$ production at extremely low transverse momentum ($p_{T} <$ 0.2 GeV/c) in hadronic Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 200 GeV and U+U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 193 GeV. Notably, the inferred nuclear modification factor of J/$\psi$ at mid-rapidity in Au+Au (U+U) collisions achieves approximately 24 (52) for $p_{T} <$ 0.05 GeV/c within the 60-80% centrality class. This significant enhancement cannot be attributed to hadronic production alongside cold or hot medium effects. Furthermore, this work provides the first-ever presentation of the $dN/dt$ distribution for J/$\psi$ in the very low $p_{T}$ regime; the distribution aligns with expectations from the Au nucleus and indicates a potential interference effect. Comparing these measurements to theoretical models of coherent production reveals that the excess yield can be reasonably described, suggesting a partial disruption of coherent production in semi-central collisions, possibly due to intense hadronic interactions. By integrating theoretical calculations, the results strongly indicate that the dramatic enhancement of J/$\psi$ yield at extremely low $p_{T}$ stems from coherent photon-nucleus interactions. Specifically, coherently produced J/$\psi$'s in violent hadronic collisions may offer a new method for probing the quark-gluon plasma.

This paper addresses the challenge of identifying intentional traffic discrimination on the Internet. Due to the Internet's complexity, detecting such discrimination is difficult, and existing tools face significant limitations. We examine the difficulties in spotting these violations, particularly within HTTPS traffic, and explore potential mitigation strategies. Our analysis centers on `Wehe`, the latest tool designed to detect net-neutrality breaches. `Wehe` aggregates traffic from key services onto a single server and replays it to simulate original server behavior. Although `Wehe` holds substantial utility and may influence policy, its mechanisms lack external validation. In this study, we identify critical flaws in `Wehe` where its replayed traffic fails to be correctly classified as intended services by network middleboxes. We substantiate this finding using a commercial traffic shaper. Furthermore, we propose a novel method that configures the SNI parameter appropriately during the initial TLS handshake to address this deficiency. Validation using commercial traffic shapers confirms that this approach enables middleboxes to correctly classify replayed traffic as intended. Consequently, our method offers a more realistic framework for detecting neutrality violations in HTTPS traffic.

Slow-roll inflation occurring at ultra-high energy scales is generally thought to be sensitive to high-order curvature corrections to classical general relativity (GR). This paper investigates the impact of the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) term on the primordial scalar and tensor spectra within the consistent $D \to 4$ Einstein Gauss-Bonnet (4EGB) gravity framework. In this context, the GB term is integrated into gravitational dynamics by re-scaling the GB coupling constant as $\alpha \to \alpha/(D-4)$ in the $D \to 4$ limit. To achieve this, we explicitly compute the primordial scalar and tensor power spectra, including GB corrections accurate to the next-to-leading order in the slow-roll approximation, utilizing the third-order uniform asymptotic approximation method. Furthermore, we calculate the corresponding spectral indices, their runnings for both scalar and tensor perturbations, and the ratio between scalar and tensor spectra, all up to the next-to-leading order in slow-roll expansions. These findings constitute the most precise results currently available in the literature.

This paper offers a qualitative examination of potentially flawed outputs generated by contextualized embedding-based techniques for identifying diachronic semantic change. We first introduce an ensemble method that surpasses prior contextualized approaches, which then serves as the foundation for a detailed analysis of predicted semantic shifts in English vocabulary over five decades. Our results indicate that these methods frequently assign high change scores to words that are not actually undergoing genuine diachronic semantic shifts, or where the validity of such shifts is dubious. We provide detailed discussions of these challenging instances with specific examples and propose corresponding linguistic classifications. Ultimately, we conclude that pre-trained contextualized language models tend to conflate changes in lexicographic senses with variations in contextual frequency, a bias inherent to their distributional nature that differs from issues seen in static embedding methods. Furthermore, these models often blend syntactic and semantic features of lexical items. Finally, we suggest several potential future solutions to address these problems.

Aerial manipulators (AM) are characterized by highly challenging non-linear dynamics, as the UAV and its attached manipulator constitute a tightly coupled system that mutually influences one another. Mathematical models of these dynamics serve as the foundation for numerous solutions in non-linear control and deep reinforcement learning. Conventional approaches typically utilize Euler angle parametrization within the Lagrangian framework or quaternion parametrization within the Newton-Euler framework; however, the former introduces singularities, while the latter suffers from algorithmic complexity. This work proposes a hybrid solution that merges the advantages of both methods: a quaternion-based approach integrated with the Lagrangian framework, thereby achieving singularity-free parameterization alongside the computational efficiency of the Lagrangian method. We provide detailed insights into the kinematic modeling and dynamic formulation of a general aerial manipulator to achieve this. The resulting dynamics model is experimentally validated against a real-time physics engine. Furthermore, we demonstrate a practical application of this model through a computed torque feedback controller (feedback linearization), analyzing its real-time performance with increasingly complex models.
This paper presents and proves several novel strong convergence theorems concerning partial sums and Fejér means associated with the Vilenkin system.

Building collaborative AI systems within probabilistic frameworks relies heavily on probabilistic user modeling. Yet, modern advanced user models, frequently structured as cognitive behavior simulators, are too computationally demanding for real-time use in cooperative AI assistants. This extended abstract tackles this issue by presenting broadly applicable differentiable surrogates that circumvent the computational bottleneck; these surrogates allow the deployment of contemporary behavioral models with an online computational cost that remains independent of the original model's complexity. Experimental results indicate that modeling performance comparable to likelihood-free inference methods is attainable, achieving an eight-order-of-magnitude reduction in computation time. Furthermore, we illustrate how AI assistants can practically integrate cognitive models in a previously examined menu-search task.

This article outlines the capabilities of Ftklipse, an extensible platform for computer forensics, and serves as a detailed specification guide for its developers. As a thick-client solution for forensic investigations, Ftklipse is built to collect, preserve, analyze, and report on digital evidence. To streamline and speed up investigations, it supports chain of custody management, access control policies, and batch operations for its integrated tools. Additionally, both the environment and its tools are configurable and are based on the Eclipse framework.

The concept that "a generator is a parser of randomness" is widely accepted folklore within the programming languages community, yet it has never been formally defined or thoroughly analyzed. This work introduces free generators, which unify parsing and generation through a shared structure that precisely defines their relationship. Free generators facilitate a proof demonstrating that many generators can be decomposed into a parser combined with a distribution over choice sequences. Additionally, they support a derivative concept analogous to Brzozowski derivatives for formal languages, enabling analysis tools to predict the impact of specific generator choices. This capability leads to a new algorithm for producing data structures that meet user-defined preconditions.

Although a rigorous mathematical framework for dimensional analysis, which systematically addresses the role of physical quantities in science and engineering, was surprisingly developed only recently, this delay has influenced contemporary mathematical models in theoretical physics. These models typically omit explicit references to units of measurement. To address this gap, we propose a novel mathematical framework: a generalization of standard algebraic structures (such as groups, rings, and vector spaces) that we term "dimensioned." This approach naturally incorporates the structure of physical dimensions. Our objective is not to establish a new algebraic theory of physical quantities, as one already exists, but rather to develop an algebraic theory grounded in the practical application of physical quantities. We conclude by examining the dimensioned analogue of Poisson algebras in detail, given their significance in Jacobi geometry and classical mechanics, with further exploration reserved for subsequent papers by the author.

Reference [12] introduced the class of partially filled arrays for cyclic groups, specifically non-zero sum Heffter arrays, which share connections with difference families, graph decompositions, and biembeddings. This work extends that definition to encompass any finite group. For a subgroup $J$ of order $t$ within a group $G$, a $\lambda$-fold non-zero sum Heffter array over $G$ relative to $J$, denoted as $^\lambda\mathrm{N}\mathrm{H}_t(m,n; h,k)$, is defined as an $m \times n$ partially filled array with entries from $G$ satisfying the following criteria: each row holds $h$ filled cells and each column holds $k$ filled cells; for every element $x \in G \setminus J$, the sum of the occurrences of $x$ and $-x$ equals $\lambda$; and, adhering to standard row and column orderings, the sum of elements in every row and column is non-zero in $G$. While [12] provided a complete probabilistic solution for the existence problem when $\lambda=1$ and $G=\mathbb{Z}_v$, serving as the foundation for this study, the current paper addresses the existence problem for arbitrary values of $\lambda$ and generic finite groups $G$. We present an almost complete solution to this problem. Specifically, utilizing local considerations inspired by the Lovász Local Lemma, we demonstrate that a $\lambda$-fold non-zero sum Heffter array over $G$ relative to $J$ exists whenever trivial necessary conditions are met and $|G|=v \geq 41$. This threshold can be lowered to $29$ if the array contains no empty cells. Furthermore, we establish that these arrays facilitate biembeddings of multigraphs into orientable surfaces and introduce new infinite families of such embeddings.

Achieving robust and high-precision quantum control is essential yet difficult for scalable quantum computation and information processing. Conventional adiabatic control faces significant performance constraints due to environmental noise, which is exacerbated by the limited coherence time of quantum systems. This study experimentally validates an alternative strategy utilizing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) on a trapped $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ ion. Specifically, we demonstrate that DRL enables rapid and robust digital quantum operations with execution times bounded by shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA). Furthermore, we show that DRL can simultaneously achieve resilience against both Rabi and detuning errors without relying on STA inputs. Our results establish a general framework for digital quantum control, offering a promising advancement for quantum information processing.

We demonstrate that multiple characteristics of the Jackiw-Teitelboim model are actually universal attributes of two-dimensional Maxwell-dilaton gravity theories across a wide range of asymptotic conditions. These theories obey a flow equation resembling a dimensionally reduced $T\bar{T}$ deformation and display chaotic dynamics, evidenced by a maximal Lyapunov exponent. A key implication of our findings is a no-go theorem that precludes smooth transitions from an asymptotically AdS$_2$ region to a de Sitter fixed point.

The Pauli Exclusion Operator (PEO) is introduced to guarantee the correct symmetry of eigenstates in multi-electron systems regarding the exchange of any pair of electrons. By incorporating the PEO into the Hamiltonian, explicit constraints on the multi-electron wave function required by the Pauli exclusion principle become unnecessary. In two-dimensional ($2D$) two-electron systems, the PEO admits a closed-form expression using momentum operators, though it acts as a non-local operator in the position representation. This work extends the concept of PEO to general multi-electron systems and examines various approximations. Analytical and numerical examples involving the PEO are provided for both isotropic and anisotropic $2D$ Hooke's atom, alongside an analysis of how approximate and kernel forms of the PEO affect energy and state calculations in this model. Finally, the connection between the PEO and standard variational methods utilizing Slater determinants is explored.

The charge density wave (CDW) order observed in the kagome superconductors KV$_3$Sb$_5$, RbV$_3$Sb$_5$, and CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ significantly influences their electronic topology. This study elucidates the temperature-dependent evolution of their structural ground states through synchrotron-based single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Both KV$_3$Sb$_5$ and RbV$_3$Sb$_5$ adopt a 2$\times$2$\times$2 superstructure within the $Fmmm$ space group, characterized by a staggered tri-hexagonal distortion of the vanadium layers. In contrast, CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ exhibits a more intricate structural progression, which was decoded using machine learning techniques applied to the scattering data. As the material cools past the CDW transition, CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ undergoes a sequential ordering process: transitioning from 2$\times$2$\times$1 and 2$\times$2$\times$2 supercells to a stable 2$\times$2$\times$4 supercell persisting down to 11 K. This final state features an average structure where vanadium layers show a coexistence of tri-hexagonal and Star of David deformation patterns. Furthermore, diffraction experiments conducted under pulsed magnetic fields up to 28 T indicate that the real component of the CDW state in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ remains unaffected by external magnetic fields.

SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanation) values are a premier method for interpreting machine learning models, offering robust theoretical properties like consistency and local accuracy alongside extensive implementation support. Although calculating SHAP values is generally exponential, TreeSHAP achieves polynomial time complexity on tree-based models. Despite this efficiency gain, TreeSHAP can still bottleneck industrial-scale solutions involving millions of data points, hindering post-hoc diagnosis and interpretation services. This paper introduces two new algorithms, Fast TreeSHAP v1 and v2, aimed at enhancing TreeSHAP's computational performance on large datasets. Empirical results indicate that Fast TreeSHAP v1 is 1.5 times faster than TreeSHAP with no increase in memory consumption. In contrast, Fast TreeSHAP v2 delivers a 2.5-fold speedup by pre-computing costly steps, at the expense of marginally higher memory usage. Furthermore, Fast TreeSHAP v2 proves highly effective for multi-time model interpretations, accelerating explanations for new incoming samples by up to three times.

The reduction of parameters has become a critical focus in deep learning, driven by the expanding scale of neural networks and the necessity to deploy them on devices with limited resources. Although numerous approaches have been explored, a rigorous theoretical foundation explaining why existing compression techniques succeed was previously missing. This paper establishes provable guarantees for certain hashing-based parameter reduction strategies. Initially, we present a compression framework utilizing random linear sketching—typically executed efficiently through hashing—demonstrating that the resulting smaller network can approximate the original on any input data drawn from smooth, well-conditioned, low-dimensional manifolds. Furthermore, this sketched network supports direct training via back-propagation. Subsequently, we analyze the HashedNets architecture, revealing that the optimization landscape of a single-hidden-layer variant exhibits a local strong convexity property akin to that of standard fully connected networks. Finally, our theoretical findings are supported by empirical validation.

An artificial gauge field for electrically neutral exciton polaritons, excluding the polarization degree of freedom, can be generated by applying crossed electric and magnetic fields. This gauge potential emerges from the motional (magneto-electric) Stark effect, which introduces a linear momentum term into the exciton's kinetic energy. We examine the interaction between this phenomenon and a competing effect caused by Rabi-splitting renormalization due to reduced electron-hole overlap in moving excitons. Accounting for this mechanism is essential in systems with high ratios of Rabi splitting to exciton binding energy. Furthermore, we propose a method to enhance the gauge field by exploiting the transition from hydrogen-like excitons to strongly dipole-polarized states under specific electric and magnetic field configurations. In this regime, the heightened sensitivity of exciton energy to momentum yields large gauge field values. As a specific case study, we analyze a GaAs ring-shaped polariton Berry phase interferometer, demonstrating that the effective magnetic flux can approach the flux quantum value within this crossover regime.

Interlayer exchange coupling (IEC) imparts distinct characteristics to synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs), rendering them ideal for various spintronic applications. However, leveraging this magnetic configuration effectively demands a deep comprehension of how magnetic properties correlate with material structure. In this work, we introduce a robust methodology for quantifying both IEC and intralayer exchange stiffness within SAFs, applying it to the ultrasmooth, amorphous Co$_{40}$Fe$_{40}$B$_{20}$ (5–40 nm)/Ru/Co$_{40}$Fe$_{40}$B$_{20}$ system. The intricate interaction between these two exchange forces generates a magnetization orientation gradient across the stack's thickness, which non-trivially modifies the hysteresis and spin wave eigenmodes. We experimentally determined the field-dependent frequencies of the first four thickness-confined spin waves and modeled these frequencies alongside their spatial profiles using micromagnetic simulations. By comparing our models with experimental data, we extracted the magnetic parameters that most accurately describe the sample's behavior. The resulting exchange stiffness is found to be 16 ± 2 pJ/m, remaining constant regardless of the Co$_{40}$Fe$_{40}$B$_{20}$ layer thickness. Meanwhile, the IEC begins at -1.7 mJ/m$^2$ for the thinnest layers and stays above -1.3 mJ/m$^2$ even for CoFeB layers up to 40 nm thick. Finally, comparing our approach with previous characterizations based solely on saturation fields suggests that tabulated IEC values for thick synthetic antiferromagnets require reevaluation.

We establish a general theorem connecting specific pushouts of $E_k$-algebras to relative tensors over $E_{k+1}$-algebras, provided the category possesses centralizers. This framework recovers several known results regarding classifying spaces, module resolutions, and (co)homology theories for ring spectra. Key applications include demonstrating that certain quotients of the dual Steenrod algebra arise as associative algebras over $HF_p \wedge HF_p$ via the attachment of a single $E_1$-algebra relation, extending earlier findings at the prime 2. Furthermore, we construct a filtered $E_2$-algebra structure on the sphere spectrum; the associated spectral sequence for stable homotopy groups of spheres features an $E_1$-term isomorphic to a regraded version of the $E_1$-term in the May spectral sequence.

Since late 2019, COVID-19 has wreaked havoc globally, significantly influencing major national and international events and media coverage. Its impact has been universal, affecting every aspect of life. As the pandemic captured global attention, social media emerged as a primary channel for worldwide discourse. Specifically, numerous individuals have utilized these platforms to share their emotions, personal experiences, and observations regarding the crisis. This study offers a comprehensive analysis of key attributes within these social media conversations concerning the novel coronavirus. We introduce a framework designed to analyze, mine, and monitor the essential content and characteristics of pandemic-related discussions. Focusing on Twitter and Reddit, we assembled a large-scale dataset of COVID-19 social media interactions. Our analysis tracks potential reports of virus transmission, symptoms, discussion topics, and linguistic complexity over time and across various regions within the United States. Additionally, we present a BERT-based model capable of identifying hateful tweets within COVID-19 discussions, achieving an error rate superior to current state-of-the-art methods. Our findings empirically validate the efficacy of our proposed framework and further illustrate that social media data can be efficiently utilized to provide public health experts with cost-effective yet thorough insights throughout an outbreak.

We introduce a complexity measure for shake-slice knots, modeled after the Morgan-Szabó definition for h-cobordisms. We demonstrate that for any non-zero framing $n$ and complexity $c \ge 1$, an $n$-shake-slice knot with complexity at least $c$ exists. Our approach utilizes dualizable patterns, and we provide a concise overview of their construction and characteristics. Furthermore, we constrain complexity by examining how the classical knot signature and the Levine-Tristram signature evolve when a single strand is twisted algebraically.

This paper introduces the Multi-scale Feature Aggregation Conformer (MFA-Conformer), a straightforward yet effective backbone for automatic speaker verification that builds upon the Convolution-augmented Transformer (Conformer). Drawing inspiration from recent state-of-the-art speech recognition and speaker verification models, the MFA-Conformer architecture incorporates three key components: a convolution subsampling layer to reduce computational costs, Conformer blocks that integrate Transformers and CNNs to effectively capture both global and local features, and a concatenation mechanism that aggregates multi-scale representations from all blocks before final pooling. Evaluations on standard benchmarks show that the best MFA-Conformer system achieves Equal Error Rates (EER) of 0.64%, 1.29%, and 1.63% on the VoxCeleb1-O, SITW.Dev, and SITW.Eval sets, respectively. These results demonstrate that MFA-Conformer significantly surpasses the popular ECAPA-TDNN system in both accuracy and inference speed. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that combining global and local feature learning yields robust and precise speaker embeddings. The project code has been made publicly available for future comparisons.

Abstract Interpretation simulates a program's concrete fixpoint calculation within an abstract domain $\mathbb{A}$. Traditionally, the abstract (post-)fixpoint process consists of two stages: an ascending phase that employs widenings to ensure termination, and a subsequent descending phase that utilizes narrowings to compensate for the precision loss caused by widenings. This paper introduces a refined variation of this standard method aimed at better restoring precision by separating these stages; specifically, prior to initiating the descending phase, the original domain $\mathbb{A}$ is substituted with a more precise domain $\mathbb{D}$. We validate the correctness of this strategy by framing it within the A$^2$I framework. Following a demonstration on a basic example, we present preliminary experimental findings, which indicate that the technique yields substantial precision gains across various selections of domains $\mathbb{A}$ and $\mathbb{D}$.

This paper employs a straightforward discrete dynamical model to investigate integer partitions and their associated lattice. We demonstrate that the set of configurations reachable under this model, when ordered by the defined transition rule, corresponds to the lattice of all integer partitions equipped with dominance ordering. First, we illustrate an algorithm capable of constructing this lattice in linear time relative to its size by leveraging its self-similar structure. Subsequently, we introduce a natural infinite extension of the model and compare it with the Young lattice. By utilizing a self-similar tree, we derive an encoding of the resulting lattice that facilitates the efficient and straightforward enumeration of all partitions for a specific integer. Furthermore, this method yields a recursive formula for calculating the total number of partitions of an integer and provides insights into specialized partition sets, including those with bounded length.

We demonstrate that if $u$ is a compactly supported distribution on the complex plane satisfying the condition that for any pair of entire functions $f$ and $g$, $\langle u,f\overline{g}\rangle=\langle u,f\rangle\langle u,\overline{g}\rangle$, then $u$ must be supported at a single point. As an application, we finalize the classification of all weighted Dirichlet spaces on the unit disk that are de Branges-Rovnyak spaces by proving that the weight function for such spaces is necessarily superharmonic.

The commercial rollout of 5G has sparked expectations for more reliable, rapid, and intelligent telecommunication systems in the next-generation Beyond 5G (B5G) radio access technologies. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are widely adopted in service-layer applications, they are also proposed as critical enablers across various B5G domains, ranging from IoT devices and edge computing to cloud infrastructures. However, existing B5G security surveys predominantly evaluate the performance and accuracy of AI/ML models, often neglecting the accountability and trustworthiness of their decisions. Explainable AI (XAI) offers a promising solution, enabling developers to uncover the internal mechanisms of these "black-box" models. Within the B5G security context, XAI aims to make automated decision-making processes transparent and understandable to stakeholders, thereby ensuring accountability for system actions. This survey highlights the role of XAI across all facets of the upcoming B5G era—including technologies like RAN, zero-touch network management, and end-to-end slicing—along with the use cases that will benefit general users. Additionally, we summarize lessons learned from recent initiatives and outline future research directions for ongoing projects involving XAI.

This study outlines Ariel Team's autonomous racing controller designed for the Indy Autonomous Challenge (IAC) simulation. As the inaugural multi-vehicle autonomous head-to-head competition, the IAC simulates high-speed racing (300 km/h) on an oval track modeled after the Indianapolis Motor Speedway (IMS). The controller's primary objectives are to advance along the track efficiently while adhering to race rules and avoiding collisions with rival vehicles. To achieve this, the system first calculates an optimal race line offline. Subsequently, it repeatedly generates a limited set of dynamically feasible maneuver candidates online, evaluating each for potential collisions with opponents. The controller then selects the maneuver that best maximizes track progress relative to the precomputed race line. Both the maneuver candidates and the predicted trajectories of opposing vehicles are approximated using a point mass model. Despite its simplicity, the controller successfully competed in the IAC final simulation race without any collisions.

The masses and spins of black holes powering Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) and producing jets can be investigated through their electromagnetic spectra. We employ the Spin-Modified Fundamental Plane of black hole activity, a non-linear relationship linking four source-frame variables: radio luminosity, X-ray or optical luminosity (derived from the [OIII] emission line), black hole mass, and spin. By incorporating uncertainties related to luminosity measurements, conversion factors, relativistic beaming, and AGN physical properties, we establish lower limits on the spins of a sample of massive, jetted AGNs.
