Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) represent a promising approach for enhancing millimeter wave (mmWave) positioning systems. This paper investigates the positioning of multiple mobile users (MUs) within RIS-aided MIMO time-division duplex (TDD) mmWave environments. We derive an expression for the space-time channel response vector (STCRV) as a new fingerprint type, which incorporates multipath channel characteristics such as time delay and angle of arrival (AOA) that correlate with the MU's location. Utilizing the STCRV as input, we introduce a novel Residual Convolution Network Regression (RCNR) algorithm to estimate the three-dimensional (3D) position of the MUs. The RCNR architecture comprises a data processing block for handling the STCRV, a standard convolution block for initial feature extraction, four residual convolution blocks to refine features while preserving their integrity, and a regression block for determining the 3D coordinates. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed RCNR algorithm outperforms traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

Byzantine State Machine Replication (SMR) has been a well-established area of study that has gained renewed interest recently due to the rise of blockchains, which companies aim to scale to hundreds of nodes. Traditional Byzantine SMRs seek to boost throughput by either minimizing the latency of sequentially executed consensus instances or by decreasing the number of replicas exchanging messages to lower network overhead. However, the first method consumes resources in bursts, while the second demands CPU-intensive authentication protocols. This paper introduces Dispel (Distributed Pipeline), a novel Byzantine SMR enabling any node to initiate new consensus instances distributively whenever local resources permit. We assessed Dispel's performance within a single datacenter and across up to 380 machines spanning three continents by benchmarking it against four other SMRs. With 128 nodes, Dispel accelerated HotStuff—Facebook's integrated Byzantine fault-tolerant SMR—by over 12 times. Furthermore, tests under both isolated and correlated failures demonstrated that Dispel's distributed architecture offers greater robustness than HotStuff. Finally, evaluations within a cryptocurrency application handling Bitcoin transactions indicate that this SMR does not constitute a performance bottleneck.

Pioneering architectures such as CLIP and DALL-E demonstrated the effectiveness of training on vast quantities of noisy image-text data, eliminating the need for costly, high-quality labels typical of traditional supervised vision learning. These models achieved robust text-guided image generation, successful transfer to downstream tasks, and exceptional zero-shot classification with strong out-of-distribution resilience. Subsequent large-scale models including ALIGN, BASIC, GLIDE, Flamingo, and Imagen have further advanced this field. However, investigating these models necessitates access to datasets comprising billions of image-text pairs, a scale that has not previously been openly shared with the research community. To democratize research into large-scale multi-modal systems, we introduce LAION-5B, a collection of 5.85 billion CLIP-filtered image-text pairs, with 2.32 billion in English. We validate the dataset's utility by successfully replicating and fine-tuning foundational models like CLIP, GLIDE, and Stable Diffusion, and outline additional experiments enabled by this open resource. Furthermore, we provide multiple nearest neighbor indices, an enhanced web interface for exploration and subset creation, and detection scores for watermarks, NSFW content, and toxicity. More information is available at https://laion.ai/laion-5b-a-new-era-of-open-large-scale-multi-modal-datasets/.

This work investigates a minimization problem within $L^p$ and $L^\infty$ spaces for specific cost functionals, where admissible mappings are restricted by the Navier-Stokes equations. Inspired by variational data assimilation for atmospheric flows in weather forecasting, we prove the existence of PDE-constrained minimizers for every $p$ and demonstrate that $L^p$ minimizers converge to $L^\infty$ minimizers as $p$ approaches infinity. Additionally, we establish that $L^p$ minimizers satisfy an Euler-Lagrange system. Finally, we show that all special $L^\infty$ minimizers derived through approximation by $L^p$ minimizers solve a divergence PDE system with measure coefficients, representing a divergence-form analogue of the corresponding non-divergence Aronsson-Euler system.

This study introduces DrugEHRQA, the inaugural question-answering dataset comprising over 70,000 question-answer pairs derived from both structured tables and unstructured notes within a publicly accessible Electronic Health Record (EHR) system. Since EHRs store patient data in formats that are not entirely disjoint—often featuring duplication, contradictions, or complementary context between these sources—our dataset specifically targets medication-related queries. To establish a baseline and facilitate dataset analysis, we developed MultimodalEHRQA, a simple model that employs a modality selection network to determine whether to route questions to table-based or text-based state-of-the-art QA models. Furthermore, to tackle challenges posed by complex, nested queries, this work represents the first application of Relation-Aware Schema Encoding and Linking for Text-to-SQL Parsers (RAT-SQL) to evaluate query template structures in EHR data. Ultimately, our objective is to create a benchmark for multi-modal QA systems and to foster new research avenues for enhancing question answering over structured EHR data by leveraging context from unstructured clinical notes.

Utilizing a (quasi)uniform magnetic field creates novel avenues for generating twisted particles with orbital angular momentum. We identify quantum states conducive to producing charged particles within a uniform magnetic field and conduct a thorough analysis of particle penetration from a solenoid into a vacuum or another solenoid. Furthermore, we outline experiments designed to successfully detect twisted positrons and positroniums. Our findings reveal a new phenomenon where the uncertainty of the particle's rotational phase increases proportionally with the distance traveled within the solenoid. This effect offers promising new methods for creating twisted particles in actual solenoids without requiring auxiliary equipment such as particle sources.

Ensuring performance and scalability while delivering services remains a pivotal challenge in web applications. The rising latency and costs associated with internet-based services have spurred the adoption of application-level caching to meet user demands and enhance the scalability and availability of origin servers. This method, where developers manually manage cached content, is employed when conventional caching strategies fall short. Despite its widespread use, application-level caching is often implemented in an ad hoc manner due to its reliance on application-specific details. Moreover, it requires developers to address a crosscutting concern distinct from the core business logic, rendering the process time-consuming, error-prone, and a frequent source of bugs. Among these challenges, determining what content to cache is particularly difficult, as it often requires frequent adjustments to accommodate application evolution and usage patterns. This paper presents an automated caching approach that identifies application-level cache content at runtime by monitoring system execution and adaptively managing caching decisions. Implemented as a framework, our solution integrates seamlessly into both new and existing web applications. Beyond reducing the development effort required for caching solutions, empirical evaluations demonstrate that our approach significantly accelerates performance and improves hit ratios, with gains ranging from 2.78% to 17.18%.

We present a new run-time approach designed to substantially minimize accuracy degradation when quantizing BERT-like architectures to 8-bit integers. Current quantization techniques typically necessitate altering the training process or implementing an extra calibration phase that relies on a specific held-out dataset. In contrast, our method enables the benefits of quantization without requiring such adjustments. We validate the effectiveness of this technique through results across multiple NLP tasks.

Although plasmas have recently emerged as subjects of study in topological materials, a complete understanding of topological phases and their transitions within cold magnetized plasmas remains elusive. This work systematically charts all such phases and confirms the bulk-edge correspondence in these systems. Our analysis reveals that the parameter space defined by density ($n$), magnetic field ($B$), and parallel wavenumber ($k_z$) contains ten distinct topological phases for linear eigenmodes. These phases are demarcated by surfaces corresponding to Langmuir wave-L wave resonance, Langmuir wave-cyclotron wave resonance, and zero magnetic field. Specifically, when $B$ and $k_z$ are held constant, only the phase transition at the Langmuir wave-cyclotron wave resonance gives rise to edge modes. We provide and numerically verify a sufficient and necessary condition for the emergence of these modes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that edge modes appear not merely at plasma-vacuum boundaries but also at more general plasma-plasma interfaces, thereby expanding the potential applications of these exotic excitations in both laboratory and space plasmas.

Knowledge graphs have become a prevalent format for storing relational data, driving the need for effective automatic reasoning techniques. This paper introduces a new method for generating a hierarchy of subject clusters, extending our previous research on taxonomy induction. The approach begins by establishing a tag hierarchy, upon which subjects are subsequently assigned to clusters. We provide quantitative evidence validating the method's capacity to create a coherent cluster hierarchy across three real-world datasets.

This study introduces a post-processing approach for enhancing the geometric details of point clouds by adapting a fractional super-resolution method to those compressed and decompressed using MPEG's G-PCC codec. Essentially, this builds upon prior work that relies solely on a down-scaled point cloud and a scaling factor, both supplied by the G-PCC codec. For non-solid point clouds, an initial down-scaling step is necessary to optimize efficiency. When compared against the G-PCC codec itself and machine-learning-based methods, the proposed method demonstrates significant quality improvements over G-PCC and achieves performance comparable to the machine-learning approaches, with

A key unresolved issue regarding massive stars is whether they are exclusively born within massive clusters or if those found in less dense regions have migrated there. The availability of wide-area digital photometric surveys now allows for the unbiased identification of massive stars outside prominent Galactic clusters. This study examines 40 candidate OB stars located in the field near the young massive cluster Westerlund 2, as identified by Mohr-Smith et al. (2017). These candidates, situated within a 1.5x1.5 square degree area, were selected based on their extinction values and K-band magnitudes. We present VLT/X-shooter spectra for two of the hottest O stars, located 11 and 22 arcminutes from the cluster center, confirming them as O4V stars with estimated masses exceeding 40 solar masses. Their radial velocities relative to the non-binary reference MSP 182 in Westerlund 2 are -29.4 +/- 1.7 km/s and -14.4 +/- 2.2 km/s, respectively. Utilizing Gaia DR2 proper motions, we determine that between 8 and 11 early O/WR stars in the surveyed region—including the two VLT targets, WR 20c, and WR 20aa—may have been ejected from Westerlund 2 within the last million years, indicating an ejection efficiency of up to 25%. The sky positions and proper motions of these stars exhibit a near north-south alignment. We discuss the potential that these findings result from the combination of prior sub-cluster merging and dynamical ejection.

Code generation models have demonstrated remarkable performance but often lack robustness, as minor prompt modifications can drastically alter their outputs. This stability is crucial for real-world deployment yet remains poorly understood. While prior research has largely addressed robustness in classification tasks for text and code, the domain of generative robustness remains unexplored, lacking a comprehensive benchmark. This paper introduces ReCode, a holistic evaluation framework designed specifically for code generation. It features over 30 custom transformations targeting docstrings, identifiers, syntax, and formatting, all engineered to remain natural within coding practices while preserving semantic intent. Human validation confirmed that more than 90% of these perturbations maintain the original meaning. Furthermore, we establish robustness metrics based on worst-case performance across perturbation types, leveraging code execution as an objective evaluation method. Experiments on state-of-the-art models using HumanEval, MBPP, and derived function completion tasks reveal that CodeGen exhibits superior robustness compared to InCoder and GPT-J, that models are most vulnerable to syntax changes, and that MBPP presents a more rigorous challenge than HumanEval.

Substantial evidence indicates that specific relaxation dynamics, such as exponential decays, occur far more frequently in nature than others. Recent efforts have sought to explain this prevalence by linking it to the stability of these common dynamics against generic Hamiltonian perturbations. This paper approaches that stability question from a novel perspective using the recursion method, specifically examining how various relaxation behaviors respond to changes in Lanczos coefficients. All investigated scenarios adhere to the "universal operator growth hypothesis." Our numerical results indicate that stability exists across a broader category of relaxation dynamics, including exponentially damped oscillations. Additionally, we introduce a criterion to distinguish "pathological" perturbations that result in atypical dynamics.

Designing detection strategies for multipartite entanglement is crucial for advancing our comprehension of fundamental quantum mechanics and has significantly influenced quantum information applications. Nevertheless, achieving accurate and robust detection methods remains a major challenge, especially as the number of nodes expands rapidly within quantum networks. In this work, we introduce a refined procedure that generates new entanglement witnesses for any targeted state using a general and operational framework. This framework is characterized by its systematic nature and high efficiency, enabling the verification of genuine multipartite entanglement across a wide range of states that occur naturally in practical settings, while vastly surpassing current standard techniques. With superior noise tolerance, our approach is highly applicable for witnessing genuine multipartite entanglement in various real-world scenarios and will aid in optimizing the utilization of entangled resources in the emerging field of quantum networks.

This research investigates how interactions with electrons, positrons, and neutrinos in the early Universe distort the equilibrium spectra of relic neutrinos. For the first time, we solve the integro-differential kinetic equations governing the neutrino density matrix, incorporating three-flavor oscillations and finite-temperature QED corrections up to the next-to-leading order $\mathcal{O}(e^3)$. Furthermore, we directly solve the equivalent kinetic equations in the neutrino mass basis and numerically assess the resulting spectral distortions, which can be readily extrapolated to determine the properties of non-relativistic neutrinos in the present-day Universe. Calculations in both bases yield an identical effective number of neutrinos, $N_{\rm eff} = 3.044$, representing the total neutrino energy density. The estimated uncertainty in this value, arising from numerical methods and neutrino mixing parameter choices, is no greater than 0.0005.

Coupling molecules to optical cavities can significantly alter their ability to absorb, transfer, and emit light, with the degree of change largely determined by the cavity-molecule coupling strength. Determining this strength across various cavity-supported modes is essential for effective cavity design. This study investigates a unique multimode dielectric microsphere, referred to as a soft-cavity, which supports both whispering gallery modes (WGM) and dark-field scattering (DFS) modes. Despite superficial similarities, these modes exhibit distinct properties, including differences in spatial electric field profiles and resonance line-widths. We examined the interaction between a monolayer of J-aggregated dye molecules and a dielectric plastic microsphere using two excitation methods: far-field excitation to generate DFS modes and evanescent excitation to generate WGMs. Our results indicate that WGMs display a clear signature of strong coupling, whereas DFS modes do not. To better interpret these findings, we compared our experimental data against a simple coupled oscillator model and conducted finite-element method numerical simulations.

A subset $A$ of the $k$-dimensional grid $\{1,2, \cdots, N\}^k$ is defined as $k$-dimensional corner-free if it contains no configuration of points $\{ a \} \cup \{ a + de_i : 1 \leq i \leq k \}$ for any $a \in \{1,2, \cdots, N\}^k$ and $d > 0$, where $e_1, \dots, e_k$ denote the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{R}^k$. Let $c_k(N)$ represent the maximum cardinality of such a corner-free subset within the grid. In this work, we demonstrate that for infinitely many values of $N$, the total number of $k$-dimensional corner-free subsets in $\{1,2, \cdots, N\}^k$ is bounded above by $2^{O(c_k(N))}$. The proof relies primarily on a supersaturation theorem regarding $k$-dimensional corners in sets of size $\Theta(c_k(N))$ combined with the hypergraph container method.

Efficient numerical methods offer valuable tools for exploring unique physical phenomena, particularly in highly frustrated quantum many-body systems. Nevertheless, calculating wave functions to accurately describe quantum states faces an exponential rise in computational complexity as the number of particles increases. In this study, we introduce a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to simulate the two-dimensional highly frustrated spin-$1/2$ $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model, achieving this at an extreme system scale with low cost and high scalability. By skillfully leveraging transfer learning and the CNN's translational invariance, we successfully analyzed a quantum system with a lattice size reaching $24\times24$ using up to 30 million cores on a new-generation Sunway supercomputer. These results validate the efficacy of CNN-based quantum-state representations and establish a new state-of-the-art benchmark, surpassing previous records in both remarkable accuracy and unprecedented system scales.

Flow through porous, elastically deformable media occurs across diverse natural scales, from geophysics to cellular biology. When constituents are incompressible, pore fluid pressure functions as a Lagrange multiplier enforcing the divergence-free constraint. This yields a potentially non-linear saddle-point system that is numerically challenging, typically necessitating nonlinear implicit solvers or flux-splitting techniques. This work introduces a simulation approach for coupled elastic deformation and flow in porous media, where pore pressure is computed at each time step by correcting trial velocities using a strategy akin to Chorin projection methods. We demonstrate the method's second-order convergence in both space and time and apply it to phase-separating neo-Hookean gels.

We analytically compute the virtual corrections for $gg\to HH$ and $gg\to ZH$ by merging an expansion in small transverse momentum with one valid at high energies. Since these two expansion methods cover complementary phase space regions, we combine their results using Padé approximants to extend the validity range of both. This approach successfully reproduces existing numerical data while maintaining exact top quark mass dependence, achieving an accuracy well below 1%. Our findings enable a rapid and adaptable calculation of the virtual corrections for these processes and are provided across various renormalization schemes for the top quark mass.

This paper primarily aims to examine the curvature characteristics of generalized pp-wave metrics. The study demonstrates that generalized pp-wave spacetimes exhibit Ricci generalized pseudosymmetry, 2-quasi-Einstein, and generalized quasi-Einstein properties according to Chaki's definitions. In a specific instance, pp-wave spacetimes are shown to be semisymmetric, semisymmetric with respect to conformal and projective curvature tensors, $R$-spaces as defined by Venzi, and satisfy the pseudosymmetric condition $P\cdot P = -\frac{1}{3}Q(S, P)$. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are explored under which a generalized pp-wave spacetime reduces to a pp-wave spacetime, pure radiation spacetime, locally symmetric, or recurrent spacetime. Additionally, it is established that the energy-momentum tensor of pp-wave spacetime is parallel if and only if it is cyclic parallel; however, while a cyclic parallel tensor is of Codazzi type, the reverse does not hold, as illustrated by a counterexample. Finally, a comparison is drawn between the curvature properties of the Robinson-Trautman metric and those of the generalized pp-wave metric.

Head tracking in head-mounted displays (HMDs) allows users to navigate a 360-degree virtual environment through unrestricted head movements. However, for seated users on chairs or couches, physically rotating 360 degrees is impossible. Redirection techniques address this by decoupling physical motion from virtual motion, offering greater flexibility in exploration. In seated scenarios limited to head movements, the discrepancy in sensory stimulation may cause detection thresholds for rotation gains to differ from those observed in redirected walking. Consequently, this study employs a two-alternative forced-choice (2AFC) experiment to compare thresholds between seated and standing conditions. Results show that users cannot distinguish rotation gains between 0.89 and 1.28, a narrower range than in standing situations. Additionally, treating head amplification as an interaction method revealed that while a gain of 2.5 is not a strict threshold, it approaches the maximum gain users find acceptable. Overall, this research seeks to enhance understanding of human perception regarding rotation gains in seated VR, providing valuable guidance for future application designs.

Combing hair entails removing topological knots within a collective curl. Through integrated experimental and computational approaches, we investigate this phenomenon, which inherently connects topology, geometry, and mechanics. Experimental observations indicate that the primary interactions in hair are two-body in nature, resembling a braided homochiral double helix. Employing this simplified model, we examine the detangling of an elastic double helix using a single rigid tine that traverses the structure, resulting in two untangled filaments behind it. Our findings quantify the correlation between detangling forces and the magnitude and spatial reach of the link density—a topological metric—that precedes the tine. Consequently, this establishes a measure for the maximum effective length of a single combing stroke, thereby illuminating the trade-offs among comfort, efficiency, and speed in the complex many-body scenario of combing a head of hair.

This paper introduces Code Shrew, a novel software platform paired with an interactive programming curriculum designed to teach fundamental coding concepts by allowing users to generate their own drawings and animations. Built on a simplified, Python-based syntax that incorporates object-oriented features for effortless drawing and animation, the environment offers an editor that responds instantly and seamlessly, fostering an engaging space for experimentation and idea testing. The accompanying course features lessons on core programming principles and progressive challenges to assess user skills, both of which leverage the editor's immediate feedback to emphasize learning through practice. We detail the software and its content, outline the underlying motivations, and explore their relationship to constructionism.

Human existence is filled with articulated objects. Gaining a holistic understanding of these objects—including their appearance, structure, physical properties, and semantics—would greatly benefit numerous research fields. However, existing solutions for articulated object understanding typically rely on synthetic datasets derived from CAD models that lack physical properties, hindering effective generalization from simulation to real-world visual and robotic applications. To address this limitation, we introduce AKB-48, a large-scale Knowledge Base for articulated objects comprising 2,037 real-world 3D models across 48 categories. Each object is represented by an ArtiKG knowledge graph. To construct AKB-48, we developed the Fast Articulation Knowledge Modeling (FArM) pipeline, which can generate an ArtiKG for an articulated object in 10–15 minutes, significantly lowering the cost of real-world object modeling. Leveraging this dataset, we propose AKBNet, a novel end-to-end pipeline for Category-level Visual Articulation Manipulation (C-VAM), where we evaluate performance on three sub-tasks: pose estimation, object reconstruction, and manipulation. The dataset, source code, and models will be made publicly available at https://liuliu66.github.io/articulationobjects/.

Positivity, defined as the premise that every distinct combination of confounding variables present in a population carries a non-zero probability of occurrence, can be further categorized into deterministic and stochastic forms. In this discussion, we revisit this distinction, explore its implications for nonparametric identifiability and estimability, and address strategies for handling violations of positivity. Furthermore, we connect positivity to emerging trends in machine learning and highlight the constraints of data-adaptive algorithms in causal inference. Although positivity is frequently neglected, it remains a critical component of valid inference.

The balls-into-bins process generalized to graphical settings extends the classical 2-choice model, where bins represent vertices of an arbitrary graph $G$. In this framework, each time step involves selecting an edge of $G$ uniformly at random and assigning a ball to one of its endpoints; the standard 2-choice process is recovered when $G$ is a complete graph $K_n$. For any $k(n)$-edge-connected, $d(n)$-regular graph with $n$ vertices and an arbitrary number of balls, we propose an allocation strategy that, with high probability, maintains a load gap of $O((d/k) \log^4 n \log \log n)$ between any two bins. This result establishes polylogarithmic bounds for specific structures like cycles and tori, where the classical greedy approach is suspected to yield only polynomial gaps. Furthermore, we prove an $\Omega((d/k) + \log n)$ lower bound on the achievable gap for any strategy across all graphs $G$, indicating that our method attains the optimal gap up to polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm is straightforward to implement, requiring $O(\log n)$ time per allocation, and functions as a global extension of the greedy strategy by comparing average loads over fixed vertex sets rather than individual ones. Central to our approach is the connection between designing effective allocation strategies and identifying appropriate multi-commodity flows; specifically, we utilize R\"{a}cke's cut-based decomposition tree to define orthogonal flows.

This paper explores payment incentives within financial networks characterized by interconnected liabilities, specifically advancing the field through two key dimensions: minimal clearing (often resulting from sequential payment execution) and debt seniorities (priorities). We differentiate between priorities that are determined endogenously versus those set exogenously. In scenarios involving endogenous priorities and standard (maximal) clearing, the associated games display a coalitional form of weak acyclicity; a strong equilibrium is guaranteed to exist and can be attained following a polynomial number of deviations, often aligning with optimal outcomes across diverse social welfare functions. Conversely, under minimal clearing, optimal strategy profiles may not exist even for utilitarian welfare measures, though a strong equilibrium still exists and remains reachable within a polynomial number of deviations for many strategies. In contrast, when priorities are exogenous, equilibria may fail to exist, and determining their existence is NP-hard for both minimal and maximal clearing mechanisms.

Open source software has increasingly garnered attention from researchers, developers, and corporations, with many Chinese tech firms actively adopting and releasing their own projects. However, existing research predominantly focuses on international giants like Microsoft and Google, leaving the practical impact of Chinese companies' open source initiatives underexplored. To bridge this gap, this study employs a mixed-method approach to examine the open source landscape of three major Chinese technology conglomerates: Baidu, Alibaba, and Tencent (BAT). The research analyzes the categories and traits of these projects, developer sentiments regarding open sourcing efforts, and the internationalization strategies employed. Data was gathered from 1,000 BAT projects on GitHub and a survey of 101 developers involved in these projects. Key findings reveal that: 1) BAT predominantly open source frontend development projects; 2) 88% of respondents hold a positive view of open sourcing within their organizations; 3) 64% identify gaining fame, expanding influence, and securing recruitment advantages as primary motivations; 4) the most common internationalization effort is providing English readme files; and 5) projects featuring English documentation tend to be more popular. These results offer valuable guidance for software engineering researchers and practical recommendations for developers and Chinese technology enterprises.

This work presents a theoretical investigation into the propagation of a Terahertz (THz) Gaussian beam through a thin, layered superconductor. In this configuration, the beam axis and the superconducting layers are oriented perpendicular to the sample interface, with the beam's electric field aligned perpendicular to the layers. We demonstrate that within this specific geometry, the Josephson current flowing between the layers induces a lensing effect on the beam, preventing the divergence typically observed at the Rayleigh range. Furthermore, because of the system's nonlinearity, both the focal length and the beam waist of the transmitted light are intensity-dependent. These relationships reveal complex hysteresis behaviors that are potentially observable in experiments utilizing THz lasers.

It is established that spatial confinement of equilibrium fluctuations in systems with long-range correlations generates effective boundary forces. In this work, we demonstrate the emergence of analogous Casimir-like forces within a non-equilibrium framework characterized by flocking active matter. Specifically, we examine a two-dimensional system of self-propelled particles with alignment interactions, maintained in a bulk flocking state and confined transversely by either reflecting or partially repulsive walls. Our results indicate that a finite-size contribution to the wall pressure arises, exhibiting a slow, algebraic decay as the separation between walls increases, alongside specific universal characteristics. We interpret these findings using a hydrodynamic model for the density and velocity fields, proposing conjectures derived from our numerical data that require validation beyond the linear approximation.

This paper introduces a novel information extraction (IE) framework called text-to-table, where models trained on text-table pairs generate one or more tables that capture the essence of an input text. Unlike existing IE approaches, this setting uniquely handles the conversion of long texts into large, complex tables without requiring explicit schema definitions, making it entirely data-driven. To the best of our knowledge, this specific problem has not been previously explored. We formalize text-to-table as a sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) task, initially utilizing a seq2seq model fine-tuned from a pre-trained language model. Furthermore, we propose an enhanced method within the seq2seq framework that incorporates table constraint and table relation embeddings. Treating this task as the inverse of the well-researched table-to-text problem, we leverage four existing table-to-text datasets for experimentation. Our results demonstrate that a standard seq2seq model outperforms baseline techniques relying on relation or named entity extraction, while our proposed enhancements further improve these performance metrics. Finally, we discuss the primary challenges associated with this task, and the associated code and data can be accessed at https://github.com/shirley-wu/text_to_table.

This study provides a multi-wavelength examination of the galaxy cluster A1668, utilizing recent EVLA and Chandra observations alongside archival H$\alpha$ data. The resulting radio images reveal a compact central source measuring approximately 14 kpc at 1.4 GHz, with a luminosity of roughly $6 \cdot 10^{23}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. The spectral index between 1.4 GHz and 5 GHz averages $\sim$ -1, aligning with typical values for Brightest Cluster Galaxies (BCGs). The X-ray cooling region spans 40 kpc and possesses a bolometric cooling luminosity of $L_{\text{cool}} = 1.9\pm 0.1 \cdot 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$. We identify a $\sim$ 6 kpc displacement between the cluster BCG and the X-ray peak, as well as a $\sim$ 7.6 kpc shift between the H$\alpha$ and X-ray peaks. Our discussion of these offsets suggests that the coolest gas does not condense directly from the lowest-entropy material; rather, we propose that sloshing has drawn the cool intracluster medium (ICM) out of the core, while expanding radio galaxy lobes have displaced the H$\alpha$ filaments. Additionally, we detect two potential X-ray cavities linked to the western (cavity A) and eastern (cavity B) radio lobes. The system's cavity power and age are estimated at $P_{\text{cav}} \sim 9 \times 10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $t_{\text{age}} \sim 5.2$ Myr, respectively. When placing A1668 within the cooling luminosity-cavity power parameter space, the AGN energy injection falls within the expected scatter, indicating that offset cooling is unlikely to disrupt the AGN feedback cycle.

Machine learning techniques, particularly artificial neural networks, are increasingly integral to contemporary science, technology, and industry. Despite their high precision and complexity, these networks are susceptible to sophisticated malicious inputs termed adversarial attacks. Although this vulnerability poses a significant threat to classical neural networks, its scope within quantum machine learning remains unclear. This study evaluates the resilience of quantum machine learning models, such as quantum variational classifiers (QVC), at scale through rigorous training on diverse image datasets and various advanced adversarial strategies. Our findings indicate that QVCs demonstrate significantly improved resistance to classical adversarial attacks by identifying features invisible to classical networks, suggesting a potential quantum advantage. Conversely, and surprisingly, attacks designed for quantum networks can also mislead classical neural networks. By integrating outcomes from both quantum and classical systems, we introduce a new technology for detecting adversarial attacks. While quantum advantage in machine learning has traditionally been pursued via enhanced accuracy or computational speed, our research highlights a novel form of advantage rooted in superior model robustness. Achieving this practical advantage could resolve critical security and reliability challenges in machine learning applications across sectors like autonomous vehicles, cybersecurity, and surveillance robotics.

We present an interactive art initiative designed to bring back the individuals obscured by the isolation of the COVID-19 pandemic through the resonant power of laughter, facilitated by cutting-edge laughter synthesis techniques. Nevertheless, the ability to unconditionally produce a wide spectrum of human emotional responses in high-fidelity audio synthesis remains an unsolved challenge, posing significant hurdles for artistic implementation. To address this, we created LaughGANter, a system utilizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) to replicate the variety of human laughter. When trained on a diverse collection of laughter recordings, LaughGANter produces varied, high-quality samples and constructs a latent space optimized for emotional analysis and innovative artistic uses, including latent mixing, interpolation, and emotional transfer.

Learning causal structures for point processes based on constraints necessitates empirical validation of local independence. Current testing methods rely on stringent model assumptions, such as the requirement that the underlying data-generating mechanism is a Hawkes process devoid of latent confounders. Even within the scope of Hawkes processes, latent confounders pose a significant technical hurdle because marginalizing a process typically results in an output that is no longer a Hawkes process. To address this, we introduce an expansion technique analogous to Volterra series to model marginalized intensities. Our primary theoretical finding demonstrates that these expansions can approximate the true marginalized intensity with arbitrary precision. Leveraging this result, we propose a novel test for local independence and evaluate its performance using both simulated and real-world datasets.

This study addresses distributed estimation within a sensor network tasked with inferring the state of a linear time-invariant (LTI) Gaussian system. By introducing a lossless decomposition of the Kalman filter, the authors establish an event-based distributed estimation framework. In this setup, each sensor executes a local filter using only its own measurements, coordinated by an event-based synchronization mechanism to integrate information from neighbors. A key innovation is the decoupling of the local filter from the synchronization process, which allows for the application of a broad range of triggering strategies. This approach guarantees stable distributed estimators provided the network meets minimal connectivity and collective system observability requirements. Compared to prior work, the proposed algorithm reduces the data volume per transmission. Additionally, the findings are extendable to enable a distributed implementation of any Luenberger observer. By solving a semi-definite programming (SDP) problem, the paper presents a low-rank estimator design that optimizes the Luenberger observer gain, ensuring distributed estimation is achieved within message complexity constraints. Finally, numerical examples are included to validate the proposed methodologies.

This paper introduces a control strategy that synchronizes both space and time, designed for simultaneous tracking and formation tasks. By utilizing a polar coordinate framework, the method correlates and decouples the kinematics of the reference and actual states between the self-vehicle and the target, thereby separating time and space to enable independent control. Consequently, the desired state is reached at a predetermined terminal time, while the spatial relative trajectory remains independent of time. Furthermore, to ensure stability prior to the designated time, a cascaded prescribed-time control theorem is established as a foundation for vehicle tracking. The derived results can be readily extended to handle simultaneous tracking and formation involving multiple vehicles. Finally, numerical simulations are presented to validate the efficacy and advantages of the proposed approach.

This study explores muonic LiH as a novel phase in $\mu$-catalyzed fusion. Utilizing three- and four-body approximations, we compute the bound states and corresponding wave functions for muonic LiH and LiH$^+$. By employing the Gaussian expansion method to solve the Schrödinger equation, we determine both the eigenenergies and wave functions, confirming the existence of bound states in these systems. Our analysis reveals that the dynamical interactions between $^7$Li and the proton in muonic LiH and LiH$^+$ closely mirror those observed in dt$\mu_2$ and dt$\mu$, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the $\alpha$ sticking probability following nuclear fusion in muonic LiH$^+$. Our calculations indicate that the probability of an $\alpha$ particle being captured into the ground state of He$\mu$ is five times lower than that in dt$\mu$.

We present a driven introduction to the theory of categorical group actions and the local geometric Langlands program, highlighting applications—both established and novel—to the representation theory of reductive and affine Lie algebras.

Time series data, though widely utilized in practical scenarios, presents significant forecasting challenges due to its non-stationary statistical properties. These evolving characteristics lead to temporal distribution shifts that often degrade the performance of existing methods. Despite this, modeling time series from a distributional perspective remains largely unexplored. This study introduces the concept of Temporal Covariate Shift (TCS) and proposes Adaptive RNNs (AdaRNN), a framework designed to address TCS by creating a model capable of strong generalization on unseen test data. AdaRNN integrates two novel algorithms: Temporal Distribution Characterization, which effectively captures distributional information within time series, and Temporal Distribution Matching, which minimizes distributional discrepancies to facilitate adaptive learning. As a flexible framework incorporating various distributional metrics, AdaRNN demonstrates superior performance in human activity recognition, air quality forecasting, and financial analysis, achieving a 2.6% increase in classification accuracy and a 9.0% reduction in RMSE compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the study indicates that the temporal distribution matching approach can be adapted to Transformer architectures to further enhance performance.

This work outlines a method for creating infinite families of 2-spheres in simply connected 4-manifolds that are pairwise smoothly inequivalent yet topologically isotopic. The complements of these spheres possess a fundamental group meeting specific criteria, encompassing finite cyclic groups and the binary icosahedral group. These findings represent the inaugural instances of knotting phenomena within 4-manifolds exhibiting such characteristics. Additionally, examples of locally flat embedded 2-spheres situated in non-smoothable 4-manifolds are provided.

This work is set for publication in the Israel Journal of Mathematics. We investigate the mean value $\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}} \bigl|\sum_{p\le N}{}u_p e(xp)\bigr|^{\ell}$ across the complete interval $\ell \in [2,\infty)$, where $\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ constitutes a well-spaced set. Our analysis offers a seamless transition between the $\ell=2$ case and $\ell>2$, thereby refining the findings of J. Bourgain and those of B. Green and T. Tao. Furthermore, we establish a uniform Hardy-Littlewood property for prime numbers and derive a sharp upper bound for the aforementioned sum when $\mathcal{X}$ is small. Finally, these results are generalized to primes within any interval, assuming a sufficient density of primes in that range.

This study examines a cryptocurrency giveaway scam executed via YouTube live streams on May 15 and 16, 2022. The scheme involved a scammer broadcasting a pre-recorded clip of a celebrity, overlaid with an announcement of a crypto giveaway that directed viewers to a deceptive website designed to appear legitimate. The fraudster promised to instantly double any cryptocurrency donations sent to a specific wallet address and return them to the victim. Analysis of the attackers' wallet addresses reveals that they successfully siphoned substantial funds over a brief period. Following an evaluation of the attackers' techniques, tactics, and procedures, this paper outlines potential countermeasures to prevent similar fraudulent activities in the future.

We establish an existence theorem for the Backus interior problem within a Euclidean ball. This challenge involves reconstructing a harmonic function inside the ball given only the magnitude of its gradient on the boundary; the problem is notably nonlinear. Physically, this corresponds to finding the velocity potential of an incompressible, irrotational fluid within the ball using boundary measurements of the velocity field's modulus. The associated linearized problem presents an irregular oblique derivative issue, leading to a loss of derivatives and rendering standard linearization approaches for the Backus problem difficult. However, by linearizing around the vertical height solution, we demonstrate that this loss of derivatives vanishes for solutions exhibiting either axial symmetry or odd symmetry in the vertical direction. Consequently, a standard fixed-point argument becomes viable, relying on tailored weighted estimates within Hölder spaces.

We investigate the complexity of chaos and turbulence through the lens of deep neural networks by evaluating their ability to classify fluid flows as either turbulent or chaotic, alongside tasks involving noise and real-world images of cats or dogs. Our analysis assesses the relative difficulty of these classification problems and measures computational complexity at both intermediate and final network stages. Furthermore, we examine both incompressible and weakly compressible fluid flows, offering evidence for the specific features neural networks utilize to differentiate turbulence from chaos.

We examine the doublet-triplet fermionic framework within the custodial limit, focusing on a pure doublet dark matter (DM) candidate situated at the electroweak scale. Although this model is theoretically attractive, it faces stringent constraints due to the tension between DM relic density requirements and LHC measurements of the Higgs diphoton decay rate. To address the observed relic abundance, we explore two possibilities: a nonstandard cosmological history or the inclusion of additional DM particles within a broader sector. We analyze how this extended sector influences various collider observables and evaluate limits from both direct detection and indirect gamma-ray searches, including diffuse and line-like spectra. Our findings indicate that while the nonstandard cosmology scenario remains subject to experimental restrictions up to a certain threshold, significant regions of parameter space remain viable. Conversely, in the multicomponent scenario, constraints are derived solely from direct detection experiments.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, we propose the notion of an "exceptional" van Hove singularity, which emerges when strong electron-electron interactions fragment a simply connected Fermi surface into multiply connected segments. This singularity marks the contact point between these two separated Fermi surface components. We demonstrate that this exceptional singularity lies close to a standard second-order van Hove singularity, reachable by adjusting a dispersion parameter. Furthermore, we contend that for a broad range of cuprates, the endpoint of the pseudogap is reached exclusively through the activation of this exceptional van Hove singularity. The ensuing Lifshitz transition is evidenced by experimental observations of increased specific heat and nematic susceptibility.

The rapid advancement of data-driven task-oriented dialogue systems has been driven by large-scale datasets, yet progress in low-resource languages remains significantly hindered by a scarcity of high-quality data. To promote cross-lingual dialogue system technology, DSTC9 introduced a cross-lingual dialog state tracking task, which evaluates dialog state tracking modules using rich-resource training data to support low-resource languages. This paper investigates the transferability of a cross-lingual generative dialog state tracking system based on a multilingual pre-trained seq2seq model. Experiments were conducted across various settings, including joint-training and pre-training on cross-lingual and cross-ontology datasets. The study reveals limited cross-lingual transferability in these approaches and offers an in-depth investigation and discussion of these findings.

This paper introduces a new preconditioning approach for the traditional 8-point algorithm (8-PA), designed to estimate an essential matrix from 360-degree field-of-view (equirectangular) images using spherical projection. To mitigate the negative impacts of uneven feature distributions and outlier correspondences on estimation accuracy, our method optimizes a non-rigid transformation that deforms the spherical camera into a novel spatial domain. This process establishes a new constraint, yielding a more robust and precise solution for the essential matrix. Experiments involving random synthetic points, 360-degree, and fish-eye images demonstrate that this normalization enhances camera pose accuracy by approximately 20% with negligible computational overhead. Furthermore, we highlight additional advantages of our method, including a constant weighted least-squares optimization that refines the well-known Gold Standard Method (GSM) by utilizing epipolar errors in non-linear optimization, and a reduction in the number of required RANSAC iterations. Both approaches confirm that our normalization produces a more reliable, robust, and accurate result.

The proposed Beam Dump Facility (BDF) is planned for the North Area of the SPS, designed to accommodate both beam dump and fixed target experiments. Together, the SPS and this new facility aim to usher in a new era of exploration at the intensity frontier, with potential research avenues including searches for weakly interacting particles predicted by Hidden Sector models and flavour physics measurements. Initially, the facility is intended to operate in beam dump mode for the Search for Hidden Particle (SHiP) experiment. Following an initial assessment between 2014 and 2016, CERN management commissioned a three-year Comprehensive Design Study. The BDF study team has since conducted an in-depth feasibility analysis covering proton delivery, the target complex, and the underground experimental zone, which included prototyping critical subsystems and evaluating radiological and safety aspects. Furthermore, preliminary integration and civil engineering studies have been completed to establish a realistic schedule and cost estimate. This document provides a detailed overview of the proposed facility, presents the findings from these studies, and outlines a potential roadmap for a subsequent three-year Technical Design Report phase, followed by a construction period of five to six years.

One of AI's primary objectives is to develop systems capable of engaging in purposeful human dialogue to facilitate task completion, a goal that has defined the field since its inception. Although recent advancements have brought voice assistants and customer service chatbots into everyday use, creating the appearance of abundant options, most deployed systems face significant challenges in development and maintenance. This difficulty stems from the necessity of manually scripting every interaction turn, a requirement that becomes increasingly burdensome as system complexity and task volume grow. To address this, we introduce Converse, a flexible, modular, tree-based framework for task-oriented dialogue. By utilizing an and-or tree structure to model tasks, Converse enables robust multi-task management, including unique capabilities for task dependencies and switching that distinguish it from other open-source frameworks. Furthermore, the system is designed to simplify bot creation for both professional and non-professional developers. The codebase can be accessed at https://github.com/salesforce/Converse.

Deep learning is increasingly applied to diverse software engineering challenges, such as program classification and defect prediction. While this approach removes the need for manual feature engineering, the quality of the source code model remains a critical factor influencing task performance. Recent studies have primarily sought to enhance Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based models by incorporating Control Flow Graph (CFG) contextual dependencies; however, these efforts largely overlook the representation of basic blocks, which serve as the foundation of such dependencies. This paper addresses this gap by integrating AST and CFG to propose a novel source code model embedded with hierarchical dependencies. Furthermore, we designed a neural network leveraging a graph attention mechanism. Specifically, we incorporated the syntactic structure of basic blocks—represented by their corresponding ASTs—into the model to provide comprehensive information. We evaluated this approach across three practical software engineering tasks against state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate significant performance gains; for instance, compared to the top-performing baseline, our model reduces parameter count by 50% while achieving a 4% accuracy improvement in program classification.

Nonlinear cascades of low-frequency Alfvénic fluctuations (AFs) are considered a potential energy source for heating plasma during the non-adiabatic expansion of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), despite the scarcity of literature reporting AFs within ICMEs. This study examines AFs inside ICMEs using Voyager 2 data from 1 to 6 au. Results indicate that AFs with high Alfvénicity occurred frequently inside ICMEs in nearly all identified events (30 out of 33), accounting for 12.6% of the total ICME duration. Generally, the percentage of AF duration decreases linearly as ICMEs expand outward. The occurrence rate of AFs within ICMEs is significantly lower than in the ambient solar wind, particularly within 4 au. Furthermore, AFs are more commonly found at the boundaries and in the center of ICMEs, a distribution pattern that mirrors the proton temperature profile. These findings imply that AFs make a substantial contribution to local plasma heating inside ICMEs.

We seek minimal extensions to the Standard Model that incorporate vector-like fermions to achieve precision unification of gauge couplings, taking into account constraints regarding proton decay, Higgs stability, and perturbativity. The most straightforward models feature multiple copies of vector fermions within two distinct (incomplete) representations. Certain variants of these models include a Type III seesaw mechanism for generating neutrino masses, while others provide a dark matter candidate; notably, in every model, at least one candidate transforms under a non-trivial representation of $SU(3)_{color}$. In the limit where Yukawa couplings vanish, new QCD bound states emerge that are detectable at the LHC. Current limits derived from 13 TeV data already constrain these particles to masses near the TeV scale. Furthermore, we demonstrate examples of similar models constructed with three or four vector representations.

We apply a numerical model from existing literature to simulate the evolution of a galaxy comprising four distinct matter components: a dark-matter halo, a rotating stellar disk, a spherical stellar bulge, and a molecular gas ring. Our results demonstrate that this galaxy model remains stable for at least 10 billion years ($10^9$ years). We characterize the final configuration using circular velocity and angular momentum distributions, tangential and radial velocity components, peak density evolution, and radial density profiles. Furthermore, we compute several equal-mass binary galaxy collision scenarios, including frontal and oblique collisions (with an impact parameter), two models initialized with 2-body orbital conditions, and a very close passage. To facilitate comparison with the single galaxy model, we analyze the collision dynamics using analogous metrics. Finally, we determine de Vaucouleurs fitting curves for the radial density profiles of all collision models over a 0–100 kpc scale. Additionally, to examine radial mass and surface density profiles at a finer resolution of 0–20 kpc, we employ a four-parameter fitting curve.

Exploration continues to be a primary hurdle in reinforcement learning (RL). Nearly all current approaches rely on a single, monolithic behavior policy that evolves slowly, whereas exploratory actions in humans and animals display significant diversity, often involving rapid switching between distinct modes. This paper initiates an investigation into mode-switching, non-monolithic exploration strategies for RL. We examine various modes for switching, determine optimal time scales for these transitions, and identify effective triggers. Furthermore, we introduce practical algorithmic components that render the switching mechanism adaptive and robust, thereby ensuring flexibility without the need for extensive hyper-parameter tuning. Finally, we present a detailed and encouraging analysis on Atari environments, utilizing a two-mode exploration strategy with switches occurring at sub-episodic time scales.

Ultra-light dark matter (ULDM) has emerged as a leading candidate for cosmological dark matter. Its primary benefit lies in its ability to resolve small-scale issues within the standard cold dark matter (CDM) framework, such as the core-cusp, missing satellite, and too-big-to-fail problems, particularly when the mass is around $m \sim 10^{-22}$ eV. This article presents a straightforward, model-independent analysis utilizing SPARC data to limit the permissible ULDM mass range. Specifically, data from the galaxy ESO563-G021 provides the tightest constraint, conservatively ruling out a mass interval of $m=(0.14-3.11)\times 10^{-22}$ eV. This model-independent exclusion aligns with numerous recent bounds and implies that ULDM may fail to address the small-scale challenges it was proposed to solve.

A new precision polarimeter would significantly address the demands of upcoming high-precision experiments at facilities like the Electron Ion Collider. By leveraging the asymmetry in the spatial distribution of the spin-dependent component of synchrotron radiation, this device would serve as a valuable complement to current conventional Møller and Compton polarimeters. The proposed spin-light polarimeter utilizes a series of wiggler magnets along the beamline to generate synchrotron radiation, which is then collimated and measured by an ionization chamber. Beam polarization is quantified by analyzing the up-down spatial asymmetry within the transverse plane. The design process began with preliminary calculations to validate the concept, followed by the simulation of wiggler fringe fields using the Los Alamos National Laboratory's 2-D Poisson Superfish toolkit; these simulations confirmed that beam motion effects and their correlations were negligible. Finally, a comprehensive GEANT-4 simulation was developed to evaluate the ionization chamber's response time and assess various factors that could impede precision polarimetry. The results indicate that the Spin-Light Polarimeter would function effectively as a relative polarimeter.

Floods represent catastrophic natural events that frequently result in significant loss of life, widespread destruction of property, and severe economic instability. These impacts are particularly profound and enduring in developing nations characterized by high population density and limited resources. To mitigate damage, Early Warning Systems (EWS) continuously monitor water levels and related variables to predict flooding, while Post Disaster Needs Assessments (PDSA) are conducted by response teams to evaluate structural harm and identify optimal recovery strategies for severely affected areas. Despite these efforts, analyzing vast quantities of image and video data for both EWS and PDSA in developing regions remains a manual task performed by first responders and volunteers. We introduce FloodTransformer, a visual transformer-based model that, to our knowledge, is the first to detect and segment flooded zones from aerial disaster imagery. Additionally, we present a novel metric, Flood Capacity (FC), designed to quantify the spatial extent of water coverage and measure segmented flood areas to support EWS and PDSA efforts. Utilizing the SWOC Flood segmentation dataset, our model achieves a 0.93 mIoU, surpassing existing methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate the approach's robustness by validating its performance on unseen flood images from diverse data sources.

On compact groups, the Haar probability measure functions as a uniform distribution. This study investigates the entropy and rate distortion theory associated with this measure. It introduces novel findings and streamlined proofs regarding the convergence of convolutions on compact groups, which can be characterized as entropy approaching its maximum. Information theoretic methods and Markov chains are central to these developments, with convergence results also expressed through rate distortion functions. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that the rate of convergence is exponential.

Ball bearing joints are essential components in all rotating machinery, and identifying faults within them remains a significant challenge for both industry and research. Intelligent fault detection (IFD) involves utilizing machine learning and statistical methods to monitor machine health. This paper investigates the creation of vibration images—a preprocessing method previously employed to train convolutional neural networks for ball bearing joint IFD. The primary findings highlight the technique's robustness by testing it on an expanded dataset and analyzing the hyperparameters involved in constructing these vibration images.

Macroscopic quantum effects are pivotal in explaining enigmatic phenomena within low-temperature quantum many-body physics, where such quantumness is typically quantified by long-range entanglement across macroscopic distances. This form of entanglement not only defines new quantum phases but also acts as a vital resource for quantum computing. Consequently, a critical question emerges regarding the conditions under which long-range entanglement remains stable at room temperature. In this study, we demonstrate that bi-partite long-range entanglement is inherently unstable at any temperature and decays exponentially with distance, effectively establishing a no-go theorem for its existence. These findings align with existing observations indicating that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures persists in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations dominate. To derive these results, we introduce a novel quantum correlation metric based on the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We prove an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems at arbitrary temperatures using this metric, which connects quantum correlation to entanglement to yield our primary conclusion. Furthermore, applying our analytical methods, we derive a general bound on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and quantum Fisher information, findings that are likely to gain significant traction in quantum metrology. Ultimately, our work uncovers fundamental aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and advances the characterization of long-range entanglement.

Minimax optimization constitutes a significant category of problems found in both contemporary machine learning and established research domains. Although numerous numerical methods exist for addressing smooth convex-concave minimax issues, approaches for nonsmooth variants remain scarce. This study introduces an efficient numerical algorithm tailored for structured nonsmooth convex-concave minimax problems. The proposed method, known as the majorized semi-proximal alternating coordinate method (mspACM), approximates the smooth component of the objective function using a majorized quadratic convex-concave function and incorporates semi-proximal terms within each subproblem. This design ensures that subproblems at every iteration are solvable, and can be solved effortlessly with appropriate selection of these semi-proximal terms. We establish the global convergence of mspACM under mild assumptions, eliminating the need for strong convexity-concavity conditions. Furthermore, assuming local metrical subregularity of the solution mapping, we demonstrate that mspACM achieves a linear convergence rate. Initial numerical experiments are presented to confirm the algorithm's efficiency.

Discrete supervised learning tasks, such as classification, are frequently addressed by formulating a continuous surrogate problem resembling regression. By bounding the original discrepancy between the estimate and the true solution with the surrogate error, these discrete problems inherit the convergence rates established for continuous cases. However, existing methods fail to exploit the fundamental distinction that discrete problems predict discrete outputs, whereas continuous ones predict continuous values. This paper addresses that gap for general structured prediction problems, paving the way for "super fast" convergence rates—specifically, excess risk rates faster than $n^{-1}$, where $n$ represents the sample size, and potentially exponential rates under strong assumptions. First, we demonstrate this approach using nearest-neighbor predictors, extending known binary classification rates to any discrete problem within the structured prediction framework. Next, we examine kernel ridge regression, improving established $n^{-1/4}$ rates to arbitrarily fast rates determined by a parameter reflecting problem difficulty; this allows the bypassing of the curse of dimensionality under smoothness conditions.

Saddle point problems have garnered significant interest recently because of their versatility in modeling challenges across diverse fields. These issues arise in numerous applied domains, including robust and distributed optimization, game theory, and machine learning tasks such as empirical risk minimization and training generative adversarial networks. Consequently, researchers have been actively devising numerical methods to address saddle point problems under various conditions. This paper focuses on creating a numerical approach for solving saddle point problems within the non-convex uniformly-concave framework. We investigate a broad class of such problems featuring composite structures and H\"older-continuous higher-order derivatives. Our proposed solution decomposes the problem into two auxiliary optimization tasks for each variable group: an outer minimization regarding primal variables and an inner maximization concerning dual variables. To tackle the outer minimization, we employ the \textit{Adaptive Gradient Method}, which is effective for non-convex scenarios and accommodates an inexact oracle derived from approximate solutions to the inner problem. For the inner maximization, we utilize the \textit{Restarted Unified Acceleration Framework}, a system that unifies high-order acceleration techniques for minimizing convex functions with H\"older-continuous higher-order derivatives. We provide separate complexity bounds for the number of first-order oracle calls required for the outer minimization and higher-order oracle calls for the inner maximization, subsequently estimating the overall complexity of the proposed approach.

Proof-of-Work cryptocurrencies typically depend on specialized hardware, known as ASICs, to execute mining operations and maintain network security. We contend that both sellers and miners have undervalued these ASICs by focusing solely on expected returns, arguing instead that such hardware should be viewed as a bundle of financial options that transform electricity into virtual coins upon exercise. Leveraging this perspective, we present a valuation method for ASICs and contrast our derived prices with actual market rates. Contrary to the common assumption that high cryptocurrency volatility reduces ASIC value, we demonstrate the opposite: volatility substantially enhances value. Consequently, a decline in a coin's volatility could drive miners away, thereby compromising security; to mitigate this risk, we propose a novel reward mechanism. Furthermore, we design a portfolio comprising coins and bonds that replicates ASIC returns and assess its performance. Historically, the realized revenues from such portfolios have significantly exceeded those of ASICs, confirming the existence of hardware mispricing and presenting an alternative investment strategy for potential miners.

This paper outlines the design, construction, and performance of an apparatus installed in the Aberdeen Tunnel laboratory in Hong Kong to investigate spallation neutrons generated by cosmic-ray muons beneath a vertical rock overburden of 611 meter water equivalent (m.w.e.). The system consists of six horizontal layers of plastic-scintillator hodoscopes used to identify the direction and position of incoming cosmic-ray muons. Positioned between these hodoscope planes is a neutron detector containing 650 kg of liquid scintillator doped with approximately 0.06% Gadolinium by weight, which enhances the efficiency of detecting spallation neutrons. The paper also presents the apparatus's performance results.

Let $X_0$ be a non-constant random variable with finite variance. For an integer $k \ge 2$, we define a sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ governed by approximately linear recursions with small perturbations $\{\Delta_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ as follows:
$$X_{n+1} = \sum_{i=1}^k a_{n,i} X_{n,i} + \Delta_n \quad \text{for all } n\ge0$$
where $X_{n,1},\dots,X_{n,k}$ are independent copies of $X_n$, and $a_{n,1},\dots,a_{n,k}$ are real coefficients. In 2004, Goldstein established bounds on the Wasserstein distance between the standard normal distribution and the law of $X_n$, showing a convergence rate of $C \gamma^n$ for constants $C>0$ and $0 < \gamma < 1$. This paper extends those findings to a two-component model by analyzing $Z_n = X_n + Y_n$ for $n \ge 0$. Here, $\{Y_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ follows a similar approximately linear recursion structure with initial variable $Y_0$ and perturbations $\{\Lambda_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$, defined for some $\ell \ge 2$ by:
$$Y_{n+1} = \sum_{j=1}^\ell b_{n,j} Y_{n,j} + \Lambda_n \quad \text{for all } n\ge0$$
In this setup, $Y_n$ and its copies $Y_{n,1},\dots,Y_{n,\ell}$ are independent and identically distributed, while $b_{n,1},\dots,b_{n,\ell}$ are real numbers. By employing the zero bias transformation within Stein's equation, we derive a corresponding bound for $Z_n$. Furthermore, under additional assumptions that the models $(X_n,\Delta_n)$ and $(Y_n,\Lambda_n)$ are independent and that the difference in variances between $X_n$ and $Y_n$ is less than the sum of their respective perturbation variances, our results align with previous work.

Utilizing the most precise measurement of the cosmic optical background obtained from recent New Horizons LORRI images, researchers have identified a flux approximately twice as high as that predicted by deep galaxy counts alone. This discrepancy, observed at a significance level of roughly $4\sigma$, is examined to determine if it originates from axion-like dark matter decaying into monoenergetic photons. By calculating the spectral energy distribution resulting from such decays and their contribution to the LORRI-measured flux, the study identifies a specific range of masses (8–20 eV) and effective axion-photon couplings ($3\text{--}6 \times 10^{-11} \text{ GeV}^{-1}$) that could account for the excess, assuming axion-like particles constitute all dark matter. Furthermore, if this excess stems from dark-matter decay producing a photon line, upcoming line-intensity mapping surveys should detect a significant signal, enabling the differentiation of this hypothesis from alternative explanations.

**Background** In February 2020, two distinct clusters of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) were identified in Hokkaido, Japan. To detect these outbreaks, this study utilized web search query logs and smartphone location data. **Material and Methods** Initially, we anonymously identified smartphone users who accessed a web search engine (Yahoo! JAPAN Search) through its companion app to search for COVID-19 or related symptoms; these individuals were classified as Web Searchers Suspicious of Their Own Infection (WSSCI). Subsequently, we extracted the geographic locations of these WSSCI users. The study then compared the spatio-temporal distribution of WSSCI counts against the known locations of the two confirmed clusters. **Result and Discussion** Our analysis revealed that several WSSCI were detected prior to the early stages of cluster development, demonstrating the fundamental viability of this WSSCI-based methodology. However, accuracy was limited to the early stages, as results became biased following public announcements regarding the clusters. Nevertheless, in scenarios where fine-grained population statistics or other cluster-related resources are unavailable, this proposed metric offers a valuable tool for identifying emerging clusters.

The first and third authors introduced digital cubical singular homology $dH_q(X)$ for digital images, establishing analogues of classical algebraic topology results. A second homology theory, $H_q^{c_1}(X)$, was developed by the second author specifically for $c_1$-digital images, offering a significantly simpler computational approach than $dH_q(X)$. This paper demonstrates an isomorphism between $dH_q(X)$ and $H_q^{c_1}(X)$ when $X$ is a $c_1$-digital image.

This paper introduces a geometric perspective on fixed-point theory, establishing novel fixed-figure results through the concept of a $k$-ellipse within a metric space. Drawing inspiration from Caristi, Kannan, Chatterjea, and \'{C}iri\'{c} type contractions, we develop existence and uniqueness theorems for a fixed $k$-ellipse. These findings are further substantiated by illustrative examples. Finally, we demonstrate the significance of our theoretical contributions by applying them to the $S$-Shaped Rectified Linear Activation Unit ($SReLU$).

Recently introduced for signal recovery, algorithms utilizing the optimal $k$-thresholding (OT) technique differ significantly from conventional hard thresholding methods, yet their computational expenses remain prohibitively high during the current development phase. To address this limitation, this paper proposes the natural thresholding (NT) algorithm and its variants. By deriving the NT family through the first-order approximation of the regularized optimal $k$-thresholding model, these methods achieve a substantially reduced computational cost compared to OT-based approaches. Theoretical analysis confirms the guaranteed performance of NT-type algorithms for recovering signals from noisy data, provided the restricted isometry property holds and the objective function of the regularized optimal $k$-thresholding model is concave. Furthermore, empirical results demonstrate that NT-type algorithms are robust and perform comparably to several mainstream techniques for sparse signal recovery.

The strong coupling constants within hadronic multiplets serve as essential parameters that encode details about the strong interactions between participating particles. These values facilitate the construction of hadron-hadron strong potentials and provide insights into the internal structure of the involved hadrons. Inspired by the recent discovery of the doubly charmed $\Xi_{cc}$ state by LHCb, we calculate the strong coupling constants for doubly heavy spin-1/2 baryons, specifically $ \Xi^{(\prime)}_{QQ^\prime }$ and $ \Omega^{(\prime)}_{QQ^\prime}$, interacting with light pseudoscalar mesons ($ \pi $, $ K $, $ \eta $, and $ \eta^\prime $) using the light cone QCD sum rules framework. The resulting data can assist experimental teams in analyzing related datasets from hadron colliders.

Inspired by Dyatlov's findings on Fourier uncertainty principles for Cantor sets and Knutsen's analogous work on joint time-frequency representations (specifically the Gaussian-windowed STFT, which corresponds to Fock spaces), we propose a broad framework connecting localization and uncertainty. Within this setting, we establish an uncertainty principle for Cantor sets within Bergman spaces on the unit disk, where the Cantor set is constructed as a union of annuli equidistributed according to hyperbolic measure. Our results are expressed using analytic Cauchy wavelets. Similar to Knutsen's STFT analysis, our theorem provides a two-sided bound for the norm of a localization operator featuring the fractal dimension $\log 2 / \log 3$ in the exponent. Furthermore, echoing both the STFT case and Dyatlov's fractal uncertainty principle, the hyperbolic measure of the dilated iterates of the Cantor set in the disk diverges to infinity, whereas the associated norm of the localization operator converges to zero.

Prestellar cores are dense, cold, self-gravitating entities within molecular clouds that serve as the birthplaces of future stars. As they transition into the protostellar phase, they are anticipated to contain centrally concentrated dense (sub)structures that act as seeds for new stars or binary/multiple stellar systems; understanding this pivotal evolutionary stage is crucial for comprehending star formation. This study reports the detection of high-density (sub)structures on a scale of approximately 1,000 au across a sample of dense prestellar cores. Using recent ALMA observations of the Orion molecular cloud, we identified five extremely dense prestellar cores featuring central regions roughly 2,000 au in size with average densities around $10^7$ $cm^{-3}$. The masses of these central dense regions span from 0.30 to 6.89 M$_\odot$. For the first time, our higher-resolution observations (0.8$'' \sim $ 320 au) reveal that one core exhibits clear signs of fragmentation. These individual substructures or fragments measure 800 to 1,700 au in size, possess masses between 0.08 and 0.84 M$_\odot$, exhibit densities of $2 - 8\times 10^7$ $cm^{-3}$, and are separated by approximately 1,200 au.
